title: Dallas Mavericks coach raves about Kyrie Irving amid NBA offseason
description: Dusty May had many kind words for Kyrie Irving after seeing him workout this offseason.
fullText:
Although former Duke Blue Devil Kyrie Irving has garnered trade interest from contending teams this offseason, the Dallas Mavericks have expressed their desire to begin the year with him as the starting point guard, alongside another former No. 1 overall pick from Duke, Cooper Flagg. Throughout the summer, Irving has remained in the gym, working on his game after missing the entire 2025-26 season while recovering from injury.

Ahead of his return, Irving's new head coach, former Michigan Wolverines coach Dusty May, had nothing but positives for Irving.

"I've watched him work out on his own, and I've watched him play pickup, and then I've gotten feedback from others that have watched him play recently, and I couldn't be more excited to be on his team. I've been blown away," said May.

"We all know how talented Kyrie is with the ball in his hands, but to see his level of preparation, attention to detail, and IQ, it's something that I've never seen at the level that he works at."

A former NBA champion and a nine-time All-Star, Irving knows a thing or two about success in the NBA. Throughout his 14-year career, Irving holds averages of 23.7 points, 5.6 assists, 4.1 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 0.4 blocks while shooting 47.4% from the field and 39.4% from beyond the arc. While a midseason trade is not yet off the table, May will certainly be thrilled to begin the year with Irving on the roster, as his expertise can offer plenty to Dallas' young core.

title: Cathy Engelbert to retire after 7 years as WNBA commissioner
description: The WNBA will have new leadership, NBA commissioner Adam Silver announced Friday. Here's what we know
fullText:
A new leader is coming to the WNBA, NBA commissioner Adam Silver announced Friday.

Cathy Engelbert informed the league of her retirement at the end of the year, marking an end to her seven-year career. Engelbert assumed the position as WNBA commissioner in 2019 after previously becoming the first female CEO of Deloitte.

"Cathy has presided over the WNBA through the most significant period of growth in the league's 30-year history," Silver said. "We are grateful for Cathy's leadership and unwavering commitment to the advancement of women's basketball."

Engelbert will be credited with getting the transformational collective bargaining agreement across the line prior to the 2026 season, but her tenure was met with controversy along the way.

There were numerous opportunities to weigh in on important topics sooner, including the recent announcement by former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White that they'd declare for the WNBA draft challenging the transgender debate sparked previously by Sophie Cunningham comments that began in an ESPN profile.

title: Report: Kawhi Leonard trade to Raptors remains ‘on track’ after Clippers punishment
description: The Los Angeles Clippers might be destined for NBA purgatory once their historic punishment for the Kawhi Leonard endorsement scandal begins to strip them of valuable roster-building assets. Leonard, meanwhile, appears poised to escape the situation largely unscathed. An agreed-upon trade to send Leonard from the Clippers to the Toronto Raptors remains “on track to be completed” now that the ...
fullText:
The Los Angeles Clippers might be destined for NBA purgatory once their historic punishment for the Kawhi Leonard endorsement scandal begins to strip them of valuable roster-building assets.

Leonard, meanwhile, appears poised to escape the situation largely unscathed.

An agreed-upon trade to send Leonard from the Clippers to the Toronto Raptors remains "on track to be completed" now that the NBA's investigation is complete, ESPN's Shams Charania reported.

"I'm told both teams did communicate, last night, an intention to move forward," Charania said Thursday on ESPN's "Get Up."

On Wednesday, the NBA announced it was stripping the Clippers of five first-round draft picks (2029-33) and fining them $30 million for violating the league's salary cap circumvention rules, having found the team funneled money to Leonard through four endorsement deals, including one with Aspiration Partners.

Clippers owner Steve Ballmer was suspended for a year for "knowingly seeking to help Mr. Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities," the NBA said after completing a probe that it had opened last year following a report on "Pablo Torre Finds Out" podcast.

Leonard was ordered to pay $700,000 in restitution, but he was not suspended, nor was his contract voided.

And, soon, he is reportedly expected to be traded to the Raptors, who had agreed during the investigation to acquire the 35-year-old star for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and a haul of picks, including 2031 and 2033 first-rounders. The trade could not go through until the investigation concluded.

That's why ESPN insider Brian Windhorst described Leonard as an "unmitigated winner."

"He collected tens of millions of dollars in endorsement deals which are not permitted by the NBA, and he was fined $700,000 in restitution," Windhorst said on "Get Up" on Thursday. "That's the greatest investment you could ever make. It's better than a Ponzi scheme that the Aspiration guy was running, I'll tell you that."

Leonard, a two-time NBA Finals MVP, led the Raptors to a championship in 2019 during a previous, one-year stint with Toronto.

"He's very likely going to get traded to Toronto, where … he's going to get a contract extension worth tens of millions," Windhorst continued. "He's going to profit from this enormously. And my guess is, on opening night, the Toronto Raptors fans will cheer him because he won them a championship [in 2019]. He can't get on the plane to Toronto fast enough."

A seven-time All-Star, Leonard averaged 27.9 points and 6.4 rebounds per game last season.

Should the trade go through, Leonard would become the headliner on a contending Raptors team that finished as the Eastern Conference's No. 5 seed last season and employs building blocks including Scottie Barnes, R.J. Barrett and Immanuel Quickley.

The Clippers, meanwhile, would pair Ingram with point guard Darius Garland and No. 5 pick Keaton Wagler in a likely rebuild, with their draft assets set to start disappearing in 2029.

title: Clippers Send Angry Letter To Adam Silver After Shocking Ruling
description: The Los Angeles Clippers finally got an answer on the NBA's cap circumvention investigation, but it's not the one they were hoping for. Despite claiming innocence and complying with the league throughout the process, NBA Commissioner Adam Silver came down with strict penalties, including a $30 million fine, the loss of five draft picks, and
fullText:
The Los Angeles Clippers finally got an answer on the NBA's cap circumvention investigation, but it's not the one they were hoping for. Despite claiming innocence and complying with the league throughout the process, NBA Commissioner Adam Silver came down with strict penalties, including a $30 million fine, the loss of five draft picks, and suspensions for several Clippers executives.

Instead of accepting their losses, however, the Clippers plan to fight with everything they have. After making their initial statement today, they shared their official email to the Commissioner, in which they called him out on the way this investigation was conducted. According to the Clippers, they worked tirelessly to comply with the league office, committing millions of dollars and many hours to prove their innocence.

"Almost one year ago today, you announced that the league would be investigating podcast allegations that the Los Angeles Clippers engaged in salary cap circumvention by funneling money to Kawhi Leonard through a 'no-show' contract with a Clippers sponsor, Aspiration. In announcing that investigation, you represented that 'due process' and 'a fundamental sense of fairness' would govern the process. You made clear that the 'burden [would be] on the league' to prove any violation through actual evidence, not 'mere appearances.' And you concluded by promising that everyone involved in the investigation would be treated 'the same way I would want to be treated if people were making allegations against me.'"

"Unfortunately, none of those promises have been kept. In the last year, Steve Ballmer has spent nearly $50 million funding an investigation by Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz that has stretched far beyond the bounds of what the league set out to investigate, let alone the bounds of 'fundamental fairness.' The Clippers have produced more than 30,000 documents and provided more than 20 witnesses who have sat for 30 interviews."

"Third parties, including Clippers business partners and sponsors, have likewise provided documents, interviews, and statements to investigators. Mr. Ballmer has reimbursed the costs of at least six law firms, many of which were hired at the demand of the league's lawyers. To say the investigation has been a distraction would be an understatement—Clippers employees have spent thousands of hours scouring document repositories, phones, messaging systems, central files, and accounting records, working with counsel, and sitting for interviews. This investigation has permanently strained relationships with key Clippers stakeholders."

It's more than money and picks that the Clippers have lost. Ballmer's reputation has also taken a hit, and relations with stakeholders have been severely strained. What's worse is that the Clippers claim they were given no warning about the NBA's ruling. Up until recently, they had the impression that they'd be cleared of wrongdoing, only to be convicted without the opportunity to respond right away.

"Mr. Ballmer's reputation has been irreparably damaged as he now finds himself embroiled not only in this heavily biased investigation but in civil litigation, the Aspiration bankruptcy proceeding, and more. It seems increasingly likely that Mr. Ballmer will spend years defending himself and the team against a podcaster's baseless claims. We have already detailed for Wachtell our concerns about the ways in which this process was designed to substantiate a predetermined outcome. But suffice it to say that you would not want to be treated the way that Mr. Ballmer and Clippers personnel have been treated during the past year. To what end?"

"League counsel has acknowledged in our discussions that the league does not believe there was an agreement between the Clippers and Aspiration to funnel money to Kawhi Leonard. League counsel also agreed with the Department of Justice, the Securities and Exchange Commission, and a federal judge that Mr. Ballmer was a victim of Joe Sanberg's fraud—not a participant. Nonetheless, with less than an hour's warning and no opportunity to respond, the league has issued a report and accompanying press release purporting to conclude the exact opposite of what it has said privately. None of this comports with any fundamental sense of fairness."

The Clippers did not directly funnel money to Kawhi Leonard through these endorsement deals, but they were still far too involved in helping him secure revenue outside of his NBA contract, including no-show endorsement deals with Aspiration and Daktronics, companies once associated with Ballmer and the Clippers. According to the Clips, however, their involvement in those deals (which they call introductions) is completely legal and not outside the norm, suggesting other teams and players might have similar arrangements. They even cited the NBA's previous investigation from several years ago, which failed to find any evidence against them.

"Instead, the league is intent on punishing Mr. Ballmer and the Clippers based on an entirely new theory: that the Clippers introduced Kawhi Leonard, at his request, to certain team vendors and sponsors. Wachtell has known about these introductions for months, yet raised them only at the eleventh hour—a pivot that demonstrates the league's predetermined decision to reach an adverse finding here. But more importantly, and as you well know, such introductions are both proper and commonplace in the league. We are confident that if the league spent $50 million investigating any team, it would find plenty of instances of team personnel making introductions to both sponsors and vendors in response to player requests."

"That is unsurprising because no league rule prohibits teams from making such introductions. Indeed, the Clippers' agreement to introduce Kawhi Leonard to team sponsors and vendors was the subject of a league investigation conducted more than seven years ago—an investigation that was concluded with no penalty or finding of wrongdoing. And as you know, high-ranking league officials, including Rick Buchanan, knew the Clippers were making introductions like these, in response to a player's requests, and raised no concerns about that approach."

"There is no due process in relitigating the league's prior investigation and finding fault with behavior that the league knew about back in 2019. And retroactively punishing the Clippers for violating a rule that never existed is hardly consistent with due process."

Finally, the Clippers conclude their email with a clear and powerful show of resistance. They accuse the investigation of being heavily flawed, call out the league for not giving them a heads-up on the decision, and announce their plans to fight back with everything they have.

"This investigation has been flawed from the outset. And your decision to issue this report without any notice to the Clippers or their counsel is inexcusable. This type of witch hunt flies in the face of fundamental fairness and of the integrity of the league and of this sport that we all love. We are exploring every legal remedy to address this gross injustice."

It's clear from this lengthy email that the Clippers have no intention of accepting the NBA's ruling here. They continue to claim their innocence and take issue with how this entire investigation has played out. But after a years-long quest to discover the truth, Adam Silver is showing no signs of reversing his decision, and it raises questions as to how far the Clippers will go to avoid the crippling list of penalties.

title: LA Clippers fined $30m by NBA over Leonard scandal
description: The LA Clippers are fined $30m (£22.2m) by the NBA for violating salary rules over the acquisition of star player Kawhi Leonard.
fullText:
The LA Clippers have been fined $30m (£22.2m) by the National Basketball Association (NBA) for violating salary rules in order to funnel millions of dollars to star player Kawhi Leonard.

The fine - the largest in the league's history - comes after the NBA report said Leonard pressured the Clippers into "obtaining off-court income opportunities [and] successfully obtaining those opportunities".

The Clippers will also have to forfeit five first-round draft picks between 2029 and 2033, while owner Steve Ballmer has been suspended from all league and team activities for 12 months for his role in matters involving Leonard's sponsorship contracts during his time with the franchise.

The NBA said the Clippers had been guilty of "knowingly seeking to help Mr Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities".

NBA commissioner Adam Silver said he was "deeply disappointed" by the Clippers' "flagrant violations" of the rules and said he believed the "severity of the penalties reflects the seriousness of the violations".

Two-time NBA champion Leonard has been fined $700,000 (£518,997) by the league.

The team's president of business operations, Gillian Zucker, has been suspended for one year without pay for providing "misleading statements to investigators".

The punishments come after the NBA said its month-long investigation "found a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations by the Clippers organisation, a prior offender of the salary-cap circumvention rules".

Following the ruling, Leonard, 35, said he "accepts full responsibility" for his actions and "regrets the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family".

"I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone's part to circumvent the salary cap," he wrote on Instagram.

The two-time NBA Finals MVP joined the Clippers in 2019 and spent seven years with the franchise before leaving earlier this year.

The NBA said both the "organisation and personnel" of the Clippers will be subject to a compliance and monitoring programme overseen by the league for five years.

title: Jalen Brunson Shares How He is a ‘Star Role Player’ After Accepting Limited Responsibilities With Mavs
description: There are a number of success stories in the NBA, and Jalen Brunson is arguably one of the most relatable. fullText:
There are a number of success stories in the NBA, and Jalen Brunson is arguably one of the most relatable.

The New York Knicks star led the team to a championship after a 23-year drought. While all five members of the starting lineup played like there was no tomorrow, stepping up as heroes in each of their four wins in the final dance, Brunson played the biggest role.

He was the smallest player on the court, something critic think is his ultimate disadvantage. Still his heart was big enough to make 7-foot-4 Victor Wembanyama tremble. It was a scenario that seemed impossible for him just four years ago.

Brunson came to the league in 2018 after a successful college career with the Villanova Wildcats. The Dallas Mavericks drafted him 33rd overall, and there weren't many expectations surrounding him, especially because the Mavs selected future superstar Luka Doncic in the same draft.

He accepted that role, but how he embraced it is what made the difference.

In an interview with the Road Trippin' show, the 2026 Finals MVP shared that he saw himself in another undersized guard, J.J. Barea, when he was handed a reserve point guard role.

"My mindset was, I'm filling JJ Barea's role. He came off the bench for Dallas. He did all these great things for Dallas.," he said.

"That's where I see myself. I'm gonna work to be better, but that's where I see myself. That's where I feel like I can help this team."

He excelled in that role. By his fourth year in Dallas, he had nearly doubled his production, going from 9.3 points per game during his rookie season to 16.3 in 2022.

Brunson believes his dedication to fulfilling the responsibilities of a role player gave him more opportunities to showcase his talent.

"The more you show in your role, the longer your leash gets, the more you're able to do. People just want to say, 'Hey, I can do this, I can do that.' Well, do what's asked of you first. Perfect it. Master it," he said.

"And all of a sudden you'll be surprised of what they'll allow you to do. And you'll be surprised by yourself, like, 'oh damn, I can do this.'"

After that, he signed with the Knicks. He is now a bona fide star.

He averaged 24 points per game in his first season in the Big Apple and 28.7 points per game the following season. He has been an All-Star in each of the last three seasons.

He is no longer a role player. Now, it is the role players who base their roles around him.

title: Ex-Warriors NBA champion gives Steph Curry retirement prediction with regular season looming
description: The Golden State Warriors have rounded out their roster for the upcoming season. Former Warriors NBA champion, Steph Curry's former teammate just gave a little insight into when he thinks the four-time champion will retire.
fullText:
Ex-Warriors NBA champion gives Steph Curry retirement prediction with regular season looming originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Golden State Warriors know that Steph Curry is nearing the end of his career one way or another. The four-time NBA champion will go down as one of the greatest players to ever play the game.

Golden State and Curry have an important decision to make, as the superstar is eligible for a contract extension.

"What the terms of a new extension look like for Curry will be completely up to him, as the Warriors are prepared to offer their star whatever he wants. If Steph wants the full $136.7 million through the 2028-29 season, he will get that. If he wants to take a discount to help the team, GM Mike Dunleavy Jr. will have no problem with said deal," NBA insider Brett Siegel wrote.

When Curry agrees to the extension will also be important. If he waits, it could potentially benefit the Warriors financially and give the organization more flexibility moving forward.

"There's still players becoming contract extension eligible. By next week you'll start to see Steph Curry's name come up. On the 29th of August he's extension eligible for his contract. I have argued that it should be considered that Steph doesn't sign the extension yet. If he chooses to sign right now, he could get two years at $140 million. Obviously if that's what he says he wants, you give it to him. But if he doesn't sign his contract extension right now the Warriors could have over $100 million in salary cap space next summer," ESPN's Brian Windhorst said.

Curry, like many of the NBA's greatest players, is getting closer to retirement. Former Golden State teammate and champion Matt Barnes recently revealed how long he believes it could be until Curry calls it a career.

"I think Steph is going to ride the ship until it sinks, similar to what Kobe did," Barnes said.

The hope is that the Warriors can make one final championship run before Curry eventually retires. LeBron James is still playing at 41 years old, so Curry could very well want to extend his career for as long as possible as well.

The former MVP remains one of the best shooters in the league, and outside of some injuries, he still looks capable of performing at an elite level. With that in mind, Curry could potentially have another two or three seasons before age begins to significantly catch up with him.

title: Warriors Fans Get Massive Steph Curry Update on Contract Talks and Retirement Plans

Golden State Warriors star Steph Curry closed last season on a sour note, falling to the Phoenix Suns in the play-in tournament after Golden State stumbled to a 37-45 finish, its fewest wins since 2019-20. Now entering his 18th NBA season, the four-time champion is opening up about his future in the Bay Area, and his latest comments carry far more weight than they first appear.

Speaking with NBC Sports Bay Area at the Workday Charity Classic in Palo Alto, Curry made his intentions clear just two days after becoming eligible for a new contract extension.

The 38-year-old guard is entering the final season of his current Golden State Warriors deal, worth 62.6 million dollars, and he is now able to sign a two-year extension worth roughly 136.7 million dollars.

"There's no question I want to be here the rest of my career, and I'm pretty sure that's going to happen," Curry said. "The deal and the contract stuff will happen at the right time, and we're not letting it be a distraction from our preparation for the season, and the fact that the team we're coming back with has a lot of familiarity."

The remark leaves little doubt about where Curry sees himself long term, even though the paperwork remains unsigned. General manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. has said Golden State wants a deal finalized before the season begins, but Curry appears content to let the process play out on its own schedule rather than rushing toward a deadline.

Curry's remarks arrive as Golden State tries to move past a rough 2025-26 season that ended with a play-in loss to the Suns. Analysts have questioned whether the current roster can get Curry back to the postseason, though he seems focused on continuity rather than promises.

He is entering his 18th NBA season alongside familiar faces like Draymond Green and Al Horford, with Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody working back from knee injuries.

His wife Ayesha shares that same confidence about what comes next for the family. "I think we're going to be in for some fun surprises over the next couple of years," Ayesha Curry added.

Golden State opens training camp at BYU-Hawaii this fall, setting up a preseason slate that will offer the first look at how the roster fits together.

Golden State's preseason schedule opens October 4 against the Los Angeles Clippers, giving fans their first look at this new-look roster. With Curry firmly committed and an extension still pending, the Warriors head into camp focused on health, continuity and getting back into playoff contention this season.

title: Charlie Baker: When NFL, NBA players return to campus, everyone else pays the price
description: All four Power Conferences have signed off on the Protect College Sports Act. NCAA President Charlie Baker writes why it must be passed into law.
fullText:
The notion college sports are for college students who will move on when they complete their degree or turn pro enjoys near-universal support. But right now, that fundamental boundary is being dismantled amid a relentless wave of litigation.

In two cases, the NCAA has been ordered to allow professional basketball players to return to college basketball, despite the fact they intentionally left college to go to the NBA Draft and each played in several NBA games. In another case, a judge required the NCAA to allow an athlete to compete for a fifth school in five years. And in the past two weeks, without so much as a hearing, let alone a trial, two courts permitted NFL players to return immediately to college football. These few examples are merely the tip of the iceberg.

POWER PLAY: College football's 25 most powerful people

OP-ED: Federal antitrust protection is only workable path to saving college sports

Eligibility rules have long held a simple purpose: Ensuring a fair playing field while preserving access to the life-changing benefits college sports provide to actual college students. For decades, that standard meant allowing student-athletes four seasons of competition over five years. Recognizing the need for evolution, NCAA member schools recently updated this rule to allow up to five years of competition before age 24. However, since the start of 2025, more than 165 lawsuits have been filed seeking to tear down these basic limits.

As rosters are increasingly packed with older adults and former professionals, the most obvious consequence is an unfair matchup on the field. But the longer-term impact falls on the next generation of young athletes who will be squeezed out of the system as a result. Sidelining incoming freshmen doesn't just rob them of their roster spots or athletic scholarship opportunities — it also strips away their chance to experience the lifelong benefits of college sports. In addition, adding former professionals to rosters costs already-enrolled student-athletes valuable playing time and development opportunities during their precious years in college.

Amid this chaos, the need to pass the Protect College Sports Act is more apparent than ever. This bipartisan bill addresses the current legal instability head-on by creating one clear, fair and enforceable eligibility standard to prevent further erosion of the competitive balance that makes college sports meaningful. Crucially, the PCSA does not stop there. It also codifies important student-athlete benefits into law, including scholarship, healthcare and revenue-sharing protections. And it takes steps to protect broad opportunities, particularly in women's and Olympic sports, by establishing sport minimums and roster protections.

This balanced approach has earned the PCSA a broad consensus of support, uniting professional, Olympic and collegiate sport groups — including student-athlete leaders and conferences across all three divisions — all of whom recognize what's at stake right now for the future of college athletics.

As the Senate prepares to return from recess and the new school year begins, the urgency is higher than ever. College sports matter. They serve our nation's youth, and I believe they are the greatest human development tool in the entire world. By passing the PCSA, lawmakers can ensure they continue to benefit young generations of athletes for decades to come.

Charlie Baker is president of the NCAA.

title: A newspaper gown and an NBA tribute - Osaka's US Open fashion statement
description: Naomi Osaka has proved she knows how to make a grand entrance at Grand Slams - and has done it again at the US Open.
fullText:
The spectacular jellyfish outfit at the Australian Open. A sparkly Eiffel Tower-inspired golden dress at the French Open. The elegant all-white Japanese kimono at Wimbledon.

Naomi Osaka has proved she knows how to make a grand entrance at the Grand Slams - and her arrival at this year's US Open was always going to turn more heads.

The four-time major champion was draped in a hooded white gown - with cuttings of newspaper headlines about her career highlights sewn in - when she walked out for her first-round match against Russia's Anastasia Zakharova in New York.

Underneath was an all-black basketball-style kit in which Osaka played as she fought her way to a 7-6 (8-6) 7-6 (7-3) win over world number 101 Zakharova.

Afterwards Osaka said the on-court look was inspired by NBA legend Allen Iverson, who is widely credited for introducing a sharper focus on fashion in his sport during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

"He's a trailblazer. I think he's also someone that I look up to a lot, because he's done a lot in fashion, whether it's on purpose or not," said Osaka.

"He's shifted the way that NBA players dress. I also think the whole conversation around clothes in sports and just expressing yourself through style.

"I feel like he's someone that I look up to in that regard."

Osaka's performance on the court in Monday's night session was less stylish, however.

The Japanese 13th seed, who won the Flushing Meadows title in 2018 and 2020, faltered after a strong start and ultimately needed to dig deep to see off Zakharova.

Osaka broke at the first opportunity to take a 2-0 lead in the opener and although she was unable to convert another chance to go 4-0 ahead, still looked comfortable when she moved 5-2 up.

However, Zakharova showed heart as she rallied to take the opener into a tie-break and fought back from another early break down in the second.

Osaka's superb serve came to the fore as she opened up a commanding 5-1 lead in the second tie-break, going on to complete victory just before 00:30 local time and avoiding the need for a deciding set.

The former world number one will face the Czech Republic's Katerina Siniakova in the second round - and promised her fans there will be another sartorial surprise.

"I wanted to play well because I wanted to show you guys some more outfits," she said.

"I love expressing myself through clothes - because I don't like talking too much."

Mutombo will now be part of his first Division-I coaching staff at BYU, sharing the bench with fellow assistants Tim Fanning, John Linehan, Brandon Dunson and Chris Burgess.

title: Joe Mazzulla Gets Real on the ‘Burden and Love’ of Coaching the Celtics, Reveals Surprising Goal
description: Boston Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla has always been known for having a different mentality. He isn’t the kind of coach who is focused on cementing his own name in NBA history.
fullText:
Boston Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla has always been known for having a different mentality.

He isn't the kind of coach who is focused on cementing his own name in NBA history. Instead, his goal is centered around something far different from what most might expect.

Mazzulla has been at the helm in Boston since the 2022-23 season. Before taking over the Celtics, his only previous head-coaching experience came during a two-year stint at Fairmont State in West Virginia.

The Celtics coach has always carried an ambitious mindset, constantly looking for ways to take Boston to greater heights. However, his ultimate goal is not to build a legacy around his name or ensure he is remembered for everything he accomplished.

In an interview this week with Josh Chambers of the University of Maryland basketball program, Mazzulla revealed that his goal as the Celtics coach is, in fact, to be forgotten.

"If the people around you didn't do what they do," Mazzulla said. "I wouldn't do anything. The thing I reflect on the most is- I think you have to be willing to be forgotten. I think that's kind of my main goal."

"I want to be forgotten about. Because that means after you, it was better. I think that's what it means to be a Celtic. However long you play, coach, work for the Celtics."

Mazzulla has consistently rejected the idea of personal glory. For him, the true measure of his impact is whether the team is in a better position when his time at Boston ends.

"It's a burden and a love for being with the Celtics," Mazzulla continued. "But it's a responsibility. I think we could take that into our daily life. Can I leave it so much better that they don't remember me because the next person came and was better?"

Having guided the Celtics to their 18th NBA championship in 2024, Mazzulla has already accomplished something few coaches can boast of.

That championship also placed Mazzulla among the youngest coaches ever to win an NBA title. He became the ninth-youngest coach to accomplish the feat and the youngest since Bill Russell won a championship with Boston as a player-coach in 1969.

Following last season, Mazzulla added another major individual honor to his résumé when he was named NBA Coach of the Year, becoming just the fourth coach in franchise history to receive Coach of the Year honors.

fullText:
The biggest criticism of Luka Doncic has been his defense. His former team reportedly pointed to it as one of the reasons they traded him.

However, a former NBA player-turned-analyst has a completely different observation. He believes Doncic will eventually win a championship, but he thinks the Los Angeles Lakers' overall style of play could prevent the Slovenian superstar from winning a ring.

Channing Frye, who was famously part of the 2016 Cleveland Cavaliers team that won the NBA championship led by LeBron James, believes Doncic's ball-dominant style and high usage rate will not lead his team to an elusive championship.

Doncic has already reached the NBA Finals once during his time with the Dallas Mavericks, although they lost to the Boston Celtics.

"I think Luka will win a championship," the retired NBA player said in his own podcast Channing's Mailbag.

"I do not think that he will win with that style of play and high usage rate. He needs a team around him, sure, but he plays physical and is usually beat up by the time. Did he miss his one chance? No. I just think something's going to come around where Luka got to come to grips with like, that's not what is going to win."

Frye's take is more about the team Doncic is playing for. He believes the Lakers should continue building around the six-time All-Star and add another player who can make Doncic trust the system and believe the team will be fine even when he is not dominating every possession.

The Lakers are already building around Doncic.

The superstar, who is coming off a long layoff that caused him to miss the 2026 postseason, reportedly had a wishlist of players, and the Lakers managed to acquire some of them.

He wanted a big man he could run the pick-and-roll with, and the Lakers signed Walker Kessler to a four-year, $130 million deal. He also reportedly badly wanted Austin Reaves back, and the Lakers rewarded the undrafted guard with a lucrative contract.

The Lakers also added Kevon Looney and Sandro Mamukelashvili to help Kessler in the frontcourt, Collin Sexton as a backup point guard, and Matisse Thybulle at the two-guard position.

There were also some major omissions from last season's starting lineup. LeBron James is now with the Philadelphia 76ers after deciding to become a free agent last June. Marcus Smart signed with the Houston Rockets, while Rui Hachimura signed with the Los Angeles Clippers. DeAndre Ayton was also traded to the Washington Wizards.

title: Nets' Egor Demin doesn't make HoopsHype's top-27 shooting guard list
description: Brooklyn Nets guard Egor Demin did not make HoopsHype's top-27 shooting guard list for the 2026-27 NBA season.
fullText:
Brooklyn Nets guard Egor Demin had a solid rookie season where he showed his ability to shoot the three-pointer better than anyone, except the Nets' coaching staff, anticipated coming into last year. Since then, Brooklyn has been hoping to see more from Demin besides his long-range shooting and he looked like he was ready to do that in the summer league, but some around the league are waiting to see it during the regular season.

HoopsHype put out its list of the projected top-27 shooting guards for the upcoming 2026-27 season and Demin did not make the list or the three players that missed the cut, putting him outside the top-30. For context, the three players that just missed the cut for HoopsHype were Shaedon Sharpe of the Portland Trail Blazers, Aaron Wiggins of the Atlanta Hawks, and Brandin Podziemski of the Golden State Warriors.

Demin, 20, is coming off an impressive showing during Brooklyn's summer circuit as he showed his ability to impact the game outside of his shooting ability, which was subpar compared to how he shot the ball last season. In five games played between the California Classic and Las Vegas Summer League, Demin averaged 21.8 points, 5.2 rebounds, 3.8 assists, and 1.8 steals per game while shooting 47.3% from the field and 28.9% from behind the three-point line.

As of this writing, HoopsHype has put out its top-27 projected lists for the point guard and shooting guard spots heading into next season and thus far, Brooklyn's projected starting guards have not made the top-30. Demin seems to be set as the shooting guard while Mikel Brown Jr. will likely be the starting point guard assuming that he plays well in camp and the preseason.

With the Nets expected to be one of the worst teams in the league next season, it makes sense to see many around the league doubt how many of the players can step up to beat the odds in an improved Easter Conference. However, it's important to note that this list is a projection so Demin has every chance to come into camp and be the best version of himself that hopefully places him in the top-27 by the time next season is over.

fullText:
The Miami Heat officially introduced Klay Thompson as a member of the franchise on Tuesday.

Thompson, the four-time NBA champion, was pretty excited about the opportunity to win another championship. He was asked a variety of questions during his press conference, including his take on the famed "Heat Culture."

"It's all about winning," Thompson said. "Some people think South Florida is 18 holes and Pina Coladas but no, it's the opposite. It's very militaristic out here, and the fitness programs are really demanding."

Thompson added that it was what made him join the Heat, especially the possibility of making a playoff run.

"It's an honor to be here and I know what they've done for so many great players who left the franchise they were with, and I look forward to having the same experience as far as impacting winning," Thompson added.

The 36-year-old sharpshooter joins forces with stars like Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. They will play under the leadership of Pat Riley and the coaching of Erik Spoelstra.

GettyKlay Thompson #11 of the Miami Heat speaks to the media during an introductory press conference at Kaseya Center on August 25, 2026 in Miami, Florida.

The Dallas Mavericks were set to pay Klay Thompson $17.5 million next season. They were initially trying to trade Thompson before agreeing to a contract buyout that saw him give up around $9.8 million, as per Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.

While the Mavericks were assembling a very good team for coach Dusty May's first season, Thompson wanted to contend for a championship. The Miami Heat quickly swooped in and signed him to a two-year, $11.5 million deal. He has a player option for next season.

Thompson brings his shooting to the Heat, giving them extra spacing on the court. It was badly needed after their acquisition of Giannis Antetokounmpo, who likes to operate inside and will need to pass the ball to shooters to become even more effective.

Despite the perception of being "washed," according to some critics online, Thompson shot pretty well from 3-point range last season at 38.3%. He did shoot a career-low 39.3% from the field, but he'll likely shoot more threes under coach Erik Spoelstra's offense.

GettyMiami Heat President Pat Riley (L) and head coach Erik Spoelstra (R) pose for a photo with Giannis Antetokounmpo #7 of the Miami Heat during an introductory press conference at Kaseya Center on July 16, 2026 in Miami, Florida.

The Miami Heat now have 13 players on standard contract, which means they still have two roster spots open. They could either sign two more free agents or add more and have an open spot in the regular season.

According to NBA insider Marc Stein of The Stein Line, the Heat have several options remaining, like Nick Richards, Gabe Vincent and Keshad Johnson. Richards has reportedly been working out in Miami, while Vincent and Johnson are former Heat players.

The Heat are $5.2 million below the second apron, so they have enough money to sign two veterans on minimum deals.

Victor Wembanyama taking a discount in his rookie-scale contract makes it much more simple to build a sufficient roster around him. title: Why Klay Thompson chose to sign with Heat, Coach Erik Spoelstra amid NBA offseason suitors
description: Klay Thompson had a very specific reason for choosing the Heat led by Coach Erik Spoelstra and Giannis Antetokounmpo.
fullText:
Why Klay Thompson chose to sign with Heat, Coach Erik Spoelstra amid NBA offseason suitors originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

When an NBA player reaches the twilight of their career, they know it, and an instinct to go after the Larry O'Brien trophy kicks in. Klay Thompson feels that exact feeling right now. After two seasons with the Dallas Mavericks, he decided to join forces with the Miami Heat led by Giannis Antetokounmpo and Coach Erik Spoelstra. Why exactly did he make that call? It all came down to adding another ring to his resume.

It is no secret that Klay Thompson found his perfect match with the Heat. When Giannis Antetokounmpo is on the floor, teams typically build a wall to prevent him from scoring in the paint. How does Coach Erik Spoelstra solve this problem? Shooters.

The Heat are no stranger to this conundrum. Coach Spoelstra experienced the same situation with LeBron James. Back then, they got Shane Battier, Mike Miller, Mario Chalmers, James Jones and Ray Allen. Now, they'll do the same with Antetokounmpo after Thompson arrives.

This schematic and rotation fit makes so much sense for the Heat. In fact, Thompson posits that his aim really is to hoist the Larry O'Brien trophy once again. If it means he has to play that specific role for Coach Spoelstra and Antetokounmpo, he would gladly do it.

He even outlined other reasons for joining the Heat in his introductory press conference.

"Just the opportunity to play high-level basketball throughout the season and the chance to make a deep postseason run. Those things were so attractive to me. Obviously, you want to maximize your potential as an athlete. I've tasted winning before; there's really nothing like it. Even just getting there and failing is better than not having a shot at it... Looking at the roster, it looked like a great fit as far as me being able to space the floor," Thompson declared.

Thompson couldn't compete to his full potential after the Warriors' 2022 NBA Championship run. Stephen Curry and the Warriors couldn't make it over the hump again, despite certain acquisitions. When he moved to the Mavericks, they tanked for Cooper Flagg in one season. During his last run with them, it was also clear it was a developmental year to define their identity.

This time around, Thompson will be surrounded by other veteran stars who have been craving a Larry O'Brien trophy. All he has to do is start knocking down shots, spacing the floor, and playing tighter defense if he wants that fifth ring to land on his finger come 2027. Can he help the Heat while breaking out of his shell?

Sky owner Michael Alter met with the local media on Tuesday to discuss the incident. According to Front Office Sports' Colin Salao, Kanter's manager texted Sky general manager Jeff Pagliocca that Kanter was coming to the game. Alter said that Pagliocca has not talked to Kanter in "three or four years."

Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter is meeting with local Chicago Sky beat writers and local Chicago media.

After that, Alter made it clear that Kanter's intentions were to be "provocative and just see how much attention he could get," but added he did not know where he was sitting before the game. Alter even spoke to people who were sitting near him to get the story.

title: Kanter Freedom ejected from WNBA game over player row
description: Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom is ejected from the Women's NBA match between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever after becoming involved in a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud.
fullText:
Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from Sunday's Women's NBA match between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever after becoming involved in a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud.

Sitting at courtside, Kanter Freedom stood up with his arms outstretched and took steps towards the court after Cloud began pointing and shouting at him during a timeout.

Kanter Freedom was wearing a T-shirt emblazoned with the words "WOMAN noun. Adult human female.".

Earlier this month, he declared he would enter next season's WNBA Draft, citing the current eligibility guidelines, or lack of, for transgender women players.

Security and other Sky players intervened, before former Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics centre Kanter Freedom was escorted from the court.

He posted on X, external: "I just got kicked out of a WNBA game for supporting WOMEN! Let that sink in, AMERICA!"

Writing on Threads, external after the game, Cloud said: "To every trans kid/person, you are apart of MY community & tribe. You belong. You're loved. You're seen. You're perfect as you are & you will always be protected by me."

Kanter Freedom reportedly spoke with police officers before exiting Chicago's Wintrust Arena.

The Fever won the match 113-90.

"There's so many good things about this league and so many good things about the play of these players, that if you come to a game, you should probably come to enjoy the basketball," said Sky head coach Tyler Marsh.

"That seems pretty simple to me. I think these players deserve that and have earned that. Being a former basketball player, you should probably understand and feel that, too."

The transgender controversy surrounding the WNBA

Sex toys again thrown on court during WNBA matches

On Saturday, the Sky's win over Golden State Valkyries was one of two WNBA matches interrupted after sex toys were thrown on to the court.

There were similar incidents last season when six WNBA matches in Atlanta, New York and Los Angeles were interrupted.

USA Today, external reported the same group responsible for last year's incidents has said it will continue to disrupt WNBA games to protest against the league's policy on transgender athletes.

The WNBA operates under a collective bargaining agreement (CBA), a deal negotiated between the league and its players association (WNBPA), setting rules on matters including player salary caps, revenue sharing, benefits and overall league operations.

On player eligibility, the CBA states: "Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA."

There are no transgender athletes currently competing in the league, but intense debate in the US has been sparked by recent comments from Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham - who played in Sunday's match in Chicago - questioning the current rules.

title: New owner deal values Timberwolves and Lynx at $4.5bn
description: The Minnesota Timberwolves change owners in a deal which makes them the fourth-most expensive NBA franchise to be sold.
fullText:
The Minnesota Timberwolves have changed ownership in a deal that values the NBA franchise and their WNBA counterpart the Minnesota Lynx at a reported combined total of $4.5bn (£3.3bn).

American businessman Marc Stad has gone from being a minority investor to controlling owner, buying the majority of the stake held by co-chairman Marc Lore.

He will join Lore's business partner and former Major League Baseball star Alex Rodriguez as co-chairman.

Rodriguez confirmed the news on Friday, and said he would be increasing his investment.

ESPN, which reported the news before Rodriguez's statement, said the deal valued the franchise at $4.5bn, the fourth-largest franchise sale in NBA history.

"One of the great joys I've had in my career is spending the last few years helping build the Timberwolves and Lynx with my friend and partner Marc Lore," Rodriguez posted on social media.

"I'm very excited to announce that this incredible journey reaches a new level today.

"Marc and Elisa Stad, who have been our partners and friends since we bought the teams, will be increasing their investment and joining me as co-chairman.

"I will also be increasing my investment and spending even more time with the teams as co-chairman, Governor of the Lynx, and alternate Governor of the Timberwolves, pending league approval."

Lore and Rodriguez initially bought in to the Minnesota teams in 2021 at a $1.5bn (£1.1bn) valuation with an agreement to eventually purchase the team in full. They assumed full control of the basketball teams last year.

It becomes the second major ownership change in the NBA this month after the LA Lakers were sold in a record-breaking deal last week.

The Timberwolves reached the Western Conference last season but lost to the San Antonio Spurs.

title: Former Spurs champion says rejecting San Antonio's $10M offer was a huge mistake
description: Stephen Jackson looked back on his decision to reject the Spurs' $10 million contract, admitting it may have cost him multiple NBA championships.
fullText:
Former Spurs champion says rejecting San Antonio's $10M offer was a huge mistake originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Stephen Jackson's NBA career didn't begin exactly as he had envisioned, but the San Antonio Spurs quickly recognized his value as a reliable two-way wing. The organization believed Jackson had the tools to defend multiple positions while providing timely outside shooting alongside Tim Duncan.

After injuries limited him for most of the 2001-02 season, Jackson enjoyed a breakthrough campaign in 2002-03. Former Spurs head coach Gregg Popovich inserted him into the starting lineup, and the move paid off. Jackson averaged 12.8 points per game during the playoff, playing a key role in San Antonio's championship run.

Following that title-winning season, Jackson believed he had earned a significant payday. He was confident that he was emerging as one of the league's rising stars and declined the Spurs' three-year, $10 million contract offer in hopes of securing a larger deal elsewhere.

Looking back, Jackson admits he would make a different decision.

"I wanted my big contract," Jackson said in "All The Smoke" podcast. "I felt like I deserved a big contract… If I could rewind back, I would have took that three-year, $10 million… I would have been on a championship team."

Passing on the Spurs' offer was a gamble, but Jackson eventually recovered financially. A breakout stint with the Atlanta Hawks helped boost his value, and later trades throughout his career allowed him to earn considerably more than the contract he originally turned down.

However, Jackson believes the biggest cost wasn't financial, instead, it was the championships he may have missed.

"I probably won two more championships, then I would have got a crazy bag," Jackson said. "I didn't understand the business at the time, so I was upset with them not getting my bag."

If Jackson accepted the three-year extension, he would have remained with the Spurs from 2003 through 2006, staying alongside Tim Duncan, Manu Ginobili and Tony Parker during one of the most dominant stretches of San Antonio's dynasty.

title: Cleveland Cavaliers acquire Peyton Watson, an NBA champ with Nuggets

fullText:
Weeks after losing the LeBron James sweepstakes, the Cavaliers are securing a fallback option at the wing position by agreeing to acquire Peyton Watson in a trade involving the Denver Nuggets and other teams.

Watson and the Cavs also struck an agreement on a four-year, $88 million contract. ESPN first reported the news on Wednesday, Aug. 19. The Cavs will trade small forward Max Strus to the Los Angeles Clippers and an unprotected first-round draft pick to the Nuggets as part of the deal.

The move for Watson comes after Akron native James announced on July 24 he would sign with the Philadelphia 76ers instead of his other top suitors, the Cavs, Miami Heat and Golden State Warriors.

A first-round pick (No. 30 overall) in the 2022 NBA Draft, Watson became a restricted free agent this offseason. As a rookie, he won the 2023 NBA title with the Nikola Jokic-led Nuggets.

Watson, 23, has spent all four of his NBA seasons in Denver.

NBA free agency: Were LeBron James, Rich Paul hinting at 76ers decision all along?

The Cavs landed on Watson after falling short in the James derby and losing Dean Wade earlier in free agency. Wade, who started 14 of Cleveland's 18 playoff games at small forward this past spring, also went to Philadelphia (four years, $39 million).

The Cavs telegraphed another move on Aug. 14, when they increased their financial flexibility by sending Dennis Schroder to the Charlotte Hornets for Tre Mann in a swap of backup point guards. The Cavs also gave the Hornets cash considerations, hard capping Cleveland at the second apron.

The deal involving Watson will be a five-team trade, NBA Insider for NBA on Prime Chris Haynes reported.

Listed as 6 feet, 8 inches and 200 pounds, Watson averaged 14.6 points on 49.1% shooting from the field (41.1% on 3-pointers), 4.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 29.6 minutes during the 2025-26 regular season. Watson missed 25 of the final 30 regular-season games and did not appear in the 2026 playoffs, with the Nuggets citing a hamstring injury. He started 40 of the 54 games in which he appeared.

Watson's career regular-season averages are 8.7 points on 47.9% shooting from the floor (36.1% on 3s), 3.5 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 21.9 minutes. His career playoff averages are three points on 36.4% shooting from the field (33.3% on 3s), 2.1 rebounds and 10.4 minutes.

title: People around NBA believe Lakers can't build front office until sold
description: There is a belief around the NBA that the Lakers cannot continue to build out their front office until their ownership situation is resolved.
fullText:
After Mark Walter officially bought a majority share of the Los Angeles Lakers this past October, he began the process of modernizing how the franchise is run. A number of people were hired to important front office positions, and fans started to feel optimistic about the direction the team was headed.

But that process is now in flux after Walter agreed to sell that majority stake to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger last week. To add even more uncertainty to the whole situation, five of the six Buss siblings voted to sell their remaining 17.8% share in the Lakers to Kushner and Iger on Monday.

Although Ramona Shelburne of ESPN said that the process of mirroring how the Los Angeles Dodgers, the Major League Baseball team Walter owns, run things will continue for now, another report indicated that the progress the front office has made may be halted. Dan Woike of The Athletic wrote that the belief around the NBA is that the Lakers cannot continue to hire people for important positions until their ownership situation is resolved.

"According to a pair of league sources who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they are not authorized to publicly discuss the Lakers' internal operations, there is a belief around the NBA that the team cannot complete the buildout of its basketball operations department until the ownership situation is resolved. After laying out a vision for a pair of assistant general managers, with one focused on analytics and one focused on player scouting, the team has yet to make any inroads in pro scouting. With preseason games set to start in a little more than a month, filling a staff and getting everyone accustomed to a system was already going to be difficult. Now it feels like a distant hope more than a reality."

In recent months, Los Angeles had hired Tony Bennett, a four-time ACC Coach of the Year who coached the University of Virginia to the national championship in 2019, to be a draft advisor. Rohan Ramadas, who was described as a "literal rocket scientist" by one source, was also brought in to be an assistant general manager and focus on analytics and the salary cap.

A number of other people were hired to handle different roles in both the basketball and business side of the organization after Walter's purchase went through.

Iger told the California Post late last week that it is "premature to speculate" on any possible plans as far as hires or changes.

title: Buss trying to block her siblings' sale of family stake in Lakers
description: Los Angeles Lakers governor Jeanie Buss is trying to stop her siblings' sale of the family's remaining stake in the NBA franchise.
fullText:
Los Angeles Lakers governor Jeanie Buss is trying to block her siblings' sale of her family's remaining stake in the NBA franchise.

Josh Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, and former Disney chief executive Bob Iger agreed a deal last week to buy the controlling interest in one of the world's most iconic sports teams from Mark Walter for $12.5bn (£9.3bn).

Walter bought his share from the Buss family last year for about $10bn (£7.45bn) in a deal that ensured Jeanie remained as governor until 2030.

The Buss family, who have been either a primary or minority owner of the Lakers since 1979, released a statement on Monday saying they had voted to sell their remaining 17.8% stake to the incoming owners.

"We have decided as a family to sell the remaining Buss Family Trust shares to the Bob Iger group as part of the ongoing transaction," the statement read.

"We love the Lakers, Lakers fans and will continue to support Los Angeles; but it is time to use this opportunity to move on and exit gracefully while we still can."

However, Jeanie's lawyer has now said she plans to fight her siblings' plan to sell.

The Buss family trust comprises of Jerry Buss' six children, with Jeanie serving as the governor of the Lakers since her father's death in 2013.

Jeanie's lawyer Adam Streisand said in a letter to her five siblings that any vote for a sale "would be and is void" because her approval as one of three co-trustees, along with siblings Joey and Janie Buss, is needed for such a move.

"Co-trustees are bound to vote to ensure that the minimum 15% ownership requirement is maintained in order to ensure that Jeanie Buss may remain controlling owner," the letter said, according to ESPN, external.

"Any attempt by the co-trustees to aid or abet the co-trustees as such, would constitute a breach of trust, breach of fiduciary duty and be in contempt of court.

"On behalf of Jeanie Buss, I demand that your clients make clear publicly that Jeanie Buss is the controlling owner of the Los Angeles Lakers and that your clients shall take no action on this supposed 'vote' to sell the 17.8% stake."

Jerry Buss bought the Lakers in a $67.5m deal (£50m) in 1979 that included the Los Angeles Kings hockey team and a Los Angeles arena that is known as the Kia Forum.

After he died in 2013, ownership was passed to his six children before a deal was completed with Walter, who also owns a stake in the LA Dodgers with Chelsea chairman Todd Boehly.

The LA Lakers have 17 NBA titles - 11 of which were won under the ownership of the Buss family - one less than the record tally held by the Boston Celtics.

The deal involving Kushner comes after he was part of the recent controversy surrounding Fifa president Gianni Infantino and an aborted plan to sell off stakes in the governing body's competitions to private investors.

Thrive Eternal, an American venture capital firm founded by Kushner, was expected to lead the proposed investor group for the Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal.

If it is approved by the NBA's board of governors next month, it will become the most expensive sports team sale ever reported - and Walter will have made a quick $2.5bn (£1.9bn) profit on his investment.

Lakers have massive problem with $50M three-time NBA champion despite trading for Walker Kessler originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Los Angeles Lakers have made several major moves this offseason to set themselves up for the near future. Los Angeles made three moves in free agency right away, significantly changing the outlook of the organization.

As soon as the new league year began, the Lakers made a blockbuster move by trading for Utah Jazz big man Walker Kessler.

"The Los Angeles Lakers started the process of remaking their roster in the wake of LeBron James' decision to leave with a blockbuster trade and a trio of free agency signings Wednesday. The Lakers have not been able to add another true backup center, meaning Looney is expected to fill that role. Lake Show Life's Tyler Watts believes that could be a major problem for Los Angeles.

"This signing was a gamble. Loon was a replacement-level player last season. The Lakers clearly believe he will be better, but they need another option. Going into the season with just two true centers is a problem. If Kessler is forced to miss time, the Lakers have serious issues on defense and at the five," Watts wrote.

The Lakers need to find a better backup center, and they know it. However, the team does not have many attractive trade pieces to acquire one. Looney was once a valuable big man for the Golden State Warriors, but he is no longer the same player he was during his prime.

Looney has made $50 million throughout his career. Los Angeles loves having Kessler as its starting center, but he does have an injury history. At this point, relying on Kessler as the primary starter without a reliable backup is not a position the Lakers want to find themselves in.

title: 6 NBA teams screwed over by the schedule release
description: The idea of playing a balanced schedule is a rarity in American professional sports. An NFL team that finishes in first place in their division one year draws other first-place teams on the schedule the next year. NHL calendars lean heavily on divisional matchups and regional rivalries. MLB moved to a more balanced schedule in […]
fullText:
The idea of playing a balanced schedule is a rarity in American professional sports. An NFL team that finishes in first place in their division one year draws other first-place teams on the schedule the next year. NHL calendars lean heavily on divisional matchups and regional rivalries. MLB moved to a more balanced schedule in 2023, reducing the number of division games and increasing interleague play to even things out.

The NBA does not play a balanced schedule, but the biggest factor in an individual team's success often feels like it has more to do with the travel arrangements than who they're playing on a particular night. Trimming the NBA's 82-game regular season schedule always felt like a silver bullet for many of the league's most pressing problems. Until that happens, teams are still jetting around the country every night to try to sell out as many arenas as possible.

The 2026-27 NBA schedule came out this week. Read our take on the league's 10 biggest rivalries for the upcoming season. With a little help from Shamit Dua's NBA Schedule Dash Board, these are the teams who got hit the hardest by the schedule makers this year.

The Celtics' 16 back-to-backs are in a five-way tie for the most in the NBA. They play 22 times in a stretch of three games in four nights, which ranks as the eighth hardest in the league. They are -4 in "net rest" games, which measures who the more tired opponent is in a given game. The Celtics aren't just dealing with the loss of Jaylen Brown this season, they're also needing to navigate one of the league's hardest travel schedules. I still think the Celtics will be a regular season wins machine, and I wouldn't count them out for grabbing the No. 1 seed in the East, but the road to get there looks more daunting after the schedule release.

The Pelicans have the hardest schedule in the NBA this year. New Orleans plays a league-leading 16 back-to-backs, they're the only team in the NBA with 27 'three in four nights' stretches, and they have a -5 net rest disadvantage. The Pelicans already had the league's seventh-lowest over/under at 29.5 wins coming into the season, and it feels like it's going to be an uphill climb to even hit that number. New head coach Jamahl Mosley has his work cut out for him. After years of believing in Zion Williamson, I'm finally giving up the dream that he can be one of the NBA's best players. At this point, I'm more interested in seeing what Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen can do together.

The Bulls are one of the league-leaders with 15 back-to-backs this season. They play a stretch of three games in four nights 24 times, which is the fourth most in the league. They're -3 on "net rest," which is third-hardest in the league. The Bulls also have five time zone crossings on no rest, which is the fifth-most in the league. The first 15 games of the season are especially brutal for Chicago, with two games against Boston, two games against the Knicks, two games against the Sixers, and one game each vs. San Antonio, Minnesota, and Cleveland. The Bulls are starting yet another rebuild, but it's going to be difficult for this fanbase to be patient when the team has the third worst cumulative record in the NBA after the last nine seasons. This year is more about figuring out if they have a future star in Caleb Wilson, and seeing how Matas Buzelis and Josh Giddey develop in their third year together. The Bulls actually have a decent bench led by Leonard Miller, Jalen Smith, and Tre Jones, and they're going to need it with this type of schedule.

The Cavs missed out on LeBron James and got a tough schedule to boot. Cleveland is tied for the league-lead with 16 back-to-backs. They have 23 'three in four nights' games, which is the sixth hardest in the NBA. They're a -2 in rest advantage, also sixth hardest. The Cavs have done a whole lot of nothing this summer coming off the world's least convincing conference finals run, but there's still time to potentially land Peyton Watson or swing a big trade. I just get the sense that Cleveland's Eastern Conference rivals are passing them by … unless Evan Mobley has another leap left in him.

The Mavericks have 16 back-to-backs (tied for the most in the league), and they're at a -3 net rest advantage. It will be fascinating to see how Dallas manages Kyrie Irving as he returns from a torn ACL at age-34. The team will also have to manage Dereck Lively II, because the 22-year-old big man still hasn't been cleared to run after having foot surgery in December. I could see a world where Cooper Flagg takes a big leap and carries the Mavs to playoff contention, but it's important to remember Flagg won't turn 20 years old until just before Christmas. It might be wise for Dallas' new front office to take a more long-term view around their franchise star.

The Lakers play 15 back-to-backs. They face three games in four nights 26 times, which is the second most in the league. There's so much riding on Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves this year. Both of them dealt with injuries last year, playing 115 out of a possible 164 games. That's not going to cut it this year. Doncic and Reaves need to carry this offense every night without LeBron James around, and the Lakers probably don't want to know what happens when Quentin Grimes needs to be their first or second option for a night. Will the Lakers have a plan to save Luka in some back-to-backs? It's going to be a battle in the Western Conference every night, but the Lakers really just need him healthy for the playoffs, unlike last year.

title: Kevin Durant Pens Heartfelt Tribute After Russell Westbrook’s Retirement

fullText:
Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant wrote a heartfelt tribute to Russell Westbrook on Thursday after his longtime teammate announced his retirement.

Durant and Westbrook spent eight seasons together with the Oklahoma City Thunder and helped define an exciting era of NBA hoops. During his emotional farewell to his fellow MVP winner and scoring champion, Durant reflected fondly upon the bond and journey the two NBA icons share.

GettyRussell Westbrook and Kevin Durant were teammates for eight seasons

On Thursday, Durant wrote a lengthy message on social media recalling Westbrook's tenacity, work ethic and influence.

The full transcript of his heartfelt tribute is as follows:

"I remember asking assistant coach Mo Cheeks, what's harder to do? Workout after practice or before?? I only asked cuz by time I would get to the gym, Russ was already done in the morning and I usually got mine in after practice. Mo like, 'coming in before practice is probably harder.' Since then, it's been my routine."

"A lot of people looked at the emotions on the court and thought Russ was loud. Nah, to me, he was quiet and methodical. He led by example, and once the lights were bright, he let everything out and experienced pure freedom. It was inspiring as his teammate. Everywhere I went, I saw it inspire people from all walks of life. Crazy thing is, he didn't say much; he just showed up. For 18 years."

Durant continued by wishing Westbrook well in his post-retirement life.

"This basketball life is sacred to us as professionals; what we put into that court means everything. Some of us wish we could go back and do things with a little more intent. Some can just wipe their hands and be satisfied with the time spent. Who u gonna be? We know what zero was on. Keep inspiring in the next phase of life, champ."

"I don't care what happens, can't erase what it was. The first YNs, finals run in our early 20s, All-Star games, seeing each other get injured and bounce back, the bus rides, plane rides, card games, jokes and arguments, the whole thing, memorable!!"

Durant concluded, "To the whole Westbrook family, Nina, the kids, mama Westbrook, big Russ, Ray, Donnell, everybody from Luezinger High and UCLA and many more that I'm forgettin, much love and Congratulations on an iconic career."

GettyRussell Westbrook is a two-time scoring champion and MVP winner

As Durant pointed out, Westbrook's legacy can never be understated or diminished.

Westbrook is one of the most decorated stars in NBA history and will be remembered by his immense passion and production on the floor.

During his storied NBA career, Westbrook earned nine All-Star and All-NBA selections. The dynamic guard was a two-time scoring champion and a three-time assists champion.

Westbrook has an NBA-record 209 triple-doubles. In those 209 such games, his teams had a cumulative record of 153-56.

Westbrook was named the 2016-17 NBA Most Valuable Player. He is also a member of the NBA 75th Anniversary Team.

title: NBA schedule release: Winners & losers, including rookies, monster slates and some questionable decisions
description: Let's take stock of how things shook out on the day when every fanbase learned what lies ahead.
fullText:
The time has come. The NBA has officially dropped its 2026-27 regular-season schedule. As with anything in life, there are winners and losers — let's dive in.

Look, I'm a big fan of a good social media product. Russell Westbrook called it quits on a fruitful 18-year career and did so with aplomb, a beautifully crafted mini-movie highlighting all the best parts of his time in the NBA.

I'm also a fan of removing all of the pomp and circumstance and getting right to brass tacks with a schedule release, as well. And who better to do this with than Suns wing Dillon Brooks? Phoenix's social-media release was a hilarious breath of fresh air, a reminder that, yes, all 30 teams in fact do play against each other. Brooks, who looks anything but camera-ready, balls up the script, throws it at the camera and declares, "We play everyone," before staring directly at the camera in a manner similar to his trademark pregame ritual. It's obvious. It's brilliant.

2026-27 Phoenix Suns Schedule Release ft. The Villain 😈

📅: https://t.co/3xzH6RpMDP pic.twitter.com/xiZwZ2WzDA

I'm sure most of you are familiar with comedians/actors Keegan Michael-Key and Jordan Peele, and their old hit sketch comedy show, "Key & Peele." If not, get hip to it. For those that do remember the series, you'll immediately recall the infamous Substitute Teacher skit, featuring an enraged Key charged with taking attendance of his class. The only issue is Key is unable to pronounce anyone's name.

Introducing the Dallas Mavericks' social-media schedule release. Adding current players Dereck Lively and Max Christie to the scene — with some of the students wearing opponent team gear — was the icing on the cake in their homage to the original. Bravo.

2026-27 schedule? Here 🙋‍♀️🙋‍♂️@Ticketmaster // #MFFL pic.twitter.com/JX8umoe62J

It's one thing for the league to pivot to an earlier start time (much earlier) to kick off the regular season. But you can't have the reason you do — which involves the European market and its prime-time viewing slot — and present the international basketball fanbase with Celtics-Pistons. No disrespect to either franchise, both of whom won 56-plus games last season. But surely there could have been a bigger draw, with some actual European stars.

If the NBA truly wanted to capitalize on that day and bring in as many eyes as possible, there are better routes to take. Let's remove the current ring night from this equation temporarily. (I certainly understand the geographic storylines between the 76ers and Knicks.) But the fun in ring night comes in the opposing team waltzing in, not giving a crap about the reigning champs being crowned and raining on their parade. Concerning the Knicks, is there a better candidate out there than the Indiana Pacers? Not only do you get to highlight the return of star point guard Tyrese Haliburton, but you also re-ignite an actual rivalry.

I'm also not saying Philadelphia shouldn't be included, it absolutely should. But why not pit it against Boston? Can't think of a better emotionally slanted slate than seeing Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum square off after years of battles together. No one asked, but here's my ideal schedule:

Since there are so many different mouths the NBA has to feed concerning streaming rights, we're forced to follow a fragmented viewing experience. Nothing better than getting off after work, heading over to the local bar to wind down and asking the employees if any of the TVs have Peacock or Amazon Prime.

I love when teams have a good pulse on what's making waves for its schedule release. The name is Samuel Henderson, probably the best birdcaller I've ever seen (not a long list). Look him up. And then watch this.

The schedule is (bird) calling 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/FEItKvFPFr

Because of the structure of the NBA Cup, only eight teams will advance from the group stage to knockout play. Six winners from both conferences and two wild cards. This means there could potentially be five teams from this pool to be eliminated from the tournament.

Knicks. Cavs. 76ers. Pacers. Heat. Pacers. Something about that just feels cruel.

I'm pleased with the league's decision to move the latter stages of the competition out of Vegas — once a year is enough for the common man or woman — but why not Seattle or another city that doesn't currently have an NBA franchise? It feels like a missed opportunity playing at Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis.

With all the attention on the national television schedule, League Pass lovers might not be feeling attended to right now. I would ask that you look under your seats and pull out the piece of paper that says 11/2 on it. A quick run through some of the games …

Pistons-Hornets: Chess match featuring two of the games' brightest coaches.

Hawks-Pacers: East playoff teams are always a vibe.

Nets-Knicks: Battle of NY, featuring Julius Randle.

Wizards-Magic: I expect Washington to be competitive from the jump and all signs from Orlando indicate it has something to prove.

Celtics-Rockets: Ime Udoka's old friends, Tatum vs. Kevin Durant, possibly high-level playoff teams.

Jazz-Spurs: Victor Wembanyama against Utah's frontline should be a real treat.

Suns-Warriors: Steph Curry and Draymond Green dealing with a pesky Brooks (and Devin Booker/Jalen Green as a nice aside).

Raptors-Clippers: Which team will Kawhi be suiting up for? Legit question these days.

Heat-Lakers: Luka Dončić. Giannis Antetokounmpo. Downtown Los Angeles. Need I say more?

AJ Dybantsa (No. 1 pick) and Darryn Peterson (No. 2 pick) won't meet until the second to last day in February, well after the All-Star break. I was in the building for their first matchup in Vegas during Summer League, and the energy in the building was palpable. It's a shame we have to wait that long for a rematch.

Cam Boozer, the No. 3 pick (and my sleeper for the actual award) won't get any national TV time against either of his colleagues. If the NBA is all for promoting its young and upcoming stars, well, this is certainly one way to do it.

title: Celtics predicted to outbid Lakers, Cavs for $46M ex-Warriors NBA champion, pair with Jayson Tatum
