title: NBA Ownership Class ‘Stunned’ by Lakers Sale
description: Sources say the sale came together in just days, with no auction.
fullText:
Wednesday morning's news that Mark Walter had sold the Lakers—less than a year after buying a controlling stake in the franchise—to former Disney CEO Bob Iger and venture capital executive Josh Kushner at a $12.5 billion valuation didn't just surprise NBA fans. It shocked the sports ownership class.

"It's one of the most bizarre things I've ever seen," said a source close to dozens of sports team owners. "My phone's ringing off the hook with people saying they're stunned."

"Why would you sell a team within a year, and especially without an auction?" asked one former NBA governor. "Especially a premier asset like the Lakers."

Adding to the confusion of the sale is that in the months since taking over the Lakers, Walter and his group had begun overhauling both the business and basketball sides of the franchise, signaling a plan to hold the team for years to come. Under Walter, the Lakers hired a new president of business operations and several other front-office executives, laid off more than a dozen employees, moved their G League team from South Bay to the Coachella Valley, and agreed to a jersey patch deal. Walter, who also owns the MLB's Dodgers, even had some of his baseball executives advising president of basketball operations Rob Pelinka on how to build out the Lakers' front office.

Yet ESPN's Ramona Shelburne, who broke the news of the team's sale to Iger and Kushner, told ESPN Radio on Wednesday morning that the deal came together "in the last few days."

Shelburne says they just called Mark Walter on SUNDAY and asked if he'd consider the sale and it just came together since then https://t.co/gohF9guYcW

Multiple ownership sources who spoke with Front Office Sports wondered whether a federal investigation into Walter's business practices could be the trigger for the unprecedented sale. Along with the Dodgers, Walter and his TWG Global holding company own stakes in Chelsea F.C., the Los Angeles Sparks, the Professional Women's Hockey League and several auto racing teams.The investigation was first reported by Bloomberg in July. Bloomberg also reported Wednesday that TWG Global is trying to raise money from investors to help pay down loans tied to its insurance businesses, the same operations that have drawn the Justice Department's attention.

"It's the only reason I can think of," one ownership source said.

Walter gave no explanation for the sale in a statement provided to ESPN.

"Owning the Los Angeles Lakers has been one of the great honors of my life — an extraordinary investment, but what I will carry with me is the community, the fans, and a city that treats this team as family," he said. "I am grateful to Jeanie Buss, the Buss family, the players, and the staff for welcoming me into this chapter. The Lakers belong to Los Angeles, and I have every confidence the best is still ahead."

The sale still needs approval from the NBA's Board of Governors, which next meets in September.

The Los Angeles Lakers are to be sold for a reported record-breaking $12.5bn, external (£9.3bn) - less than a year after Mark Walter took a majority stake in the NBA franchise.

Josh Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, and former Disney chief executive Bob Iger are buying the controlling interest in one of the world's most iconic sports teams.

Walter bought his share, reportedly worth an estimated $10bn (£7.45bn) - a previous record - from the Buss family in a deal that was unanimously approved by the NBA Board of Governors in October 2025.

Kushner and Iger said in a statement: "As lifelong NBA fans, we are deeply honoured for the opportunity to become stewards of the Los Angeles Lakers, one of the most iconic sports franchises in the world.

"We have immense respect for the leadership and vision of Jerry and Jeanie Buss.

"Our long-term commitment is to build on that foundation, compete at the highest level, and serve this extraordinary team, its fans, and the city of Los Angeles."

Jerry Buss bought the Lakers in a $67.5m deal (£50m) in 1979 that included the Los Angeles Kings hockey team and a Los Angeles arena, known as the Kia Forum.

After he died in 2013, ownership was passed to his six children in a Trust before a deal was completed with Walter, who also owns a stake in the LA Dodgers with Todd Boehly.

"Owning the Los Angeles Lakers has been one of the great honors of my life," said Walter.

"It has been an extraordinary investment, but what I will carry with me is the community, the fans, and a city that treats this team as family.

"I am grateful to Jeanie Buss, the Buss family, the players, and the staff for welcoming me into this chapter. The Lakers belong to Los Angeles, and I have every confidence the best is still ahead."

The LA Lakers have 17 NBA titles - one less than the record of 18 held by the Boston Celtics.

The deal involving Kushner comes after he was part of the recent controversy surrounding Fifa president Gianni Infantino and an aborted plan to sell off stakes in the governing body's competitions to private investors.

Thrive Eternal, an American venture capital firm founded by Kushner, was expected to lead the proposed investor group for the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

The complete schedule also includes the San Antonio Spurs against the New York Knicks, the Philadelphia 76ers against the Los Angeles Lakers, the Oklahoma City Thunder against the Minnesota Timberwolves and the Denver Nuggets against the Golden State Warriors.

Every matchup offers considerable star power, but Celtics-Heat carries something the others cannot manufacture: years of genuine animosity and postseason history.

Boston and Miami have repeatedly collided with championships at stake. Their latest meeting will arrive on one of the NBA's grandest stages, giving the Celtics another national opportunity to display their reshaped roster.

Christmas dinner may have to wait in New England.

Few Eastern Conference matchups have carried more weight over the past 15 years. The Celtics and Heat met in the playoffs six times between 2010 and 2024, including four appearances in the Eastern Conference finals. Miami won the conference finals meetings in 2012, 2020 and 2023, while Boston broke through in 2022.

The rivalry added another chapter during the first round of the 2024 playoffs. Miami stunned Boston by making a franchise playoff-record 23 3-pointers in Game 2, but the Celtics responded by winning the next three games and eliminating the Heat in five. Boston went on to capture its record-setting 18th NBA championship.

The personnel surrounding the rivalry has changed over time, but the intensity has remained. Miami has consistently embraced the challenge of facing Boston, while the Celtics know better than to overlook an organization that has repeatedly caused them postseason frustration.

That history should give the Christmas Day meeting a playoff-like edge even though it will arrive relatively early in the season. Neither team will need additional motivation.

The Christmas matchup also gives the NBA another opportunity to feature Boston's new star combination. Jayson Tatum and Paul George will enter the season as the leading faces of a reworked Celtics roster. Their partnership will receive national attention immediately. Boston already is scheduled to open the season Oct. 20 against Cade Cunningham and the Detroit Pistons on NBC and Peacock. Adding a Christmas Day meeting with Miami reinforces the league's belief that the Celtics remain one of its biggest attractions.

The game also could offer a valuable measuring stick. By late December, Tatum and George should have enough time together to move beyond the adjustment stage. The Celtics' offensive roles, closing lineup and defensive identity should be clearer than they will be on opening night.

Miami will be eager to test all of it.

The Heat have built their reputation on toughness, defensive discipline and an ability to make favored opponents uncomfortable. Those traits have made them particularly dangerous against Boston, regardless of each team's regular-season record.

A Christmas win would not settle any postseason questions, but it could provide an early psychological advantage if the rivals meet again when the stakes are even higher.

Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs will face the defending champion Knicks. LeBron James and the 76ers will meet the Lakers, creating one of the day's most fascinating individual storylines.

Boston's inclusion is hardly surprising. The Celtics have become a Christmas Day fixture because of their enormous fan base, championship history and consistent place among the NBA's most prominent contenders.

The opponent makes this appearance feel different.

Miami is not just another team on Boston's schedule. The Heat are responsible for some of the Celtics' most painful playoff exits, while Boston has delivered its share of disappointment in return.

The rivalry has survived changing rosters, different coaches and shifting expectations. It now gets another national showcase with families across the country watching.

For the Celtics, Christmas Day will bring an opportunity to make another statement about their championship ambitions. For the Heat, it will offer a chance to disrupt Boston's holiday and remind the Eastern Conference that this rivalry remains as dangerous as ever.

title: The transgender row surrounding the WNBA
description: After the Indiana Fever's Sophie Cunningham said it was "common sense" to ban transgender women from women's sports, a row has emerged in the WNBA - with former NBA players saying eligibility rules mean they can enter the 2027 Draft.
fullText:
The WNBA is still in the midst of its 2026 season and yet it is next year's Draft for North America's top women's basketball league that is dominating the headlines.

Why? Because some former men's NBA players have declared they will enter for selection - citing the current eligibility guidelines, or lack of, for transgender women players.

"I'm officially declaring myself a WNBA prospect," said Enes Kanter Freedom, who played 11 seasons in the NBA.

It is the latest development in a story ignited by a comment made by Indiana Fever player Sophie Cunningham, who said she wanted to protect young girls "who shouldn't have to go against biological men" in sport.

Her words have instigated protests - albeit not grand in scale - on both sides of the argument, and once again catapulted the debate around transgender women in sport into the spotlight.

Last month, Cunningham, one of the league's most high-profile players, gave an interview to ESPN, external in which the conversation turned to the topic of "protecting" women's sports.

The Indiana Fever guard said she had received criticism from people who believed she "hated" transgender people, something she denied.

She said she wanted to "extend love" to everyone, but added: "I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."

She later doubled down on her comments, saying it was "common sense", external to bar transgender athletes from competing in women's sports.

Her words quickly moved beyond basketball and into a wider political debate in the United States.

President Donald Trump expressed his support for Cunningham, while vice-president JD Vance said she was "inspiring".

Though the 29-year-old later said she is "not a very political person", her remarks have followed her around the country. Competing rallies from critics and supporters were organised at Indiana's games, along with small-scale protests.

The scale of the debate in the media, online and in politics was striking given no openly transgender woman is due to play, or has ever played, in the WNBA.

The WNBA operates under a collective bargaining agreement (CBA), a deal negotiated between the league and its players association (WNBPA), setting rules on matters including player salary caps, revenue sharing, benefits and overall league operations.

On player eligibility, the CBA states: "Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA."

The WNBA has yet to comment publicly on the row since Cunningham's comments but league commissioner Cathy Engelbert reportedly sent a memo to teams last week in which she said the matter would be discussed at an upcoming pre-arranged meeting with team presidents.

In the memo, seen by the Associated Press, external, Engelbert said the league would "always approach this topic thoughtfully, respectfully, and in alignment with the longstanding values of our league".

She added: "Our player eligibility rules, unlike the eligibility rules of some other leagues and governing bodies, are collectively bargained. Preserving the integrity of our game and ensuring fair competition will always remain among the league's highest priorities."

However, the lack of detail in the league's eligibility criteria has been brought to light by Kanter Freedom, who finished his playing career with the Boston Celtics in 2022.

"If simply declaring who you are is all that's required, then I meet every single requirement necessary to compete in the WNBA," he wrote on Instagram, external.

Kanter Freedom, who has previously spoken out about human rights violations in China and Turkey, among other issues, added: "I know my presence on the court will stir up strong opinions. I am definitely not here to mock, make fun of, or disrespect any community or personal choices.

"I'm simply asking that the current rules be applied equally to everyone - the rules that represent the very values many WNBA players and coaches have publicly advocated for."

A day after Kanter Freedom's 'announcement', Royce White - who made three appearances in the NBA as a player and is now a Republican Senate candidate - said he would also declare for the Draft, adding: "I identify as sometimes identifying as a woman for purpose of basketball."

Whether the vagueness of the rules are by design to leave it open to transgender women or a sign of an oversight that genuinely needs tightening up is not clear.

BBC Sport has contacted Cunningham's representatives, the WNBA and WNBPA for comment.

Cunningham's comments have become a flashpoint inside a league which has a long history of player activism on issues including race, gender equality and LGBTQ+ rights.

The players' association did not mention Cunningham by name when it eventually addressed the debate.

In a statement the WNBPA denounced "hate abuse and demonisation of the transgender community" and reaffirmed its commitment to "justice, equity, diversity and inclusion".

It called on fans to report abusive behaviour at games and added that it would continue to have "hard" conversations but it "will not be used as political pawns".

There is strong feeling on both sides of the argument. Minnesota Lynx head coach and president Cheryl Reeve, who said: "I come from a space of inclusion.

"The narrative that I think is problematic is to suggest that transgender athletes are the biggest problem in women's sports."

Reeve wore a "Trans Kids Belong" T-shirt before Minnesota played Indiana earlier this month and was seen speaking to Cunningham on court before the game.

Cunningham later said the pair had exchanged their perspectives and that the conversation ended with "love and respect".

Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams said she would welcome a transgender athlete "on my team or against my team, any time".

Last month, the WNBA suspended Seattle Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton from attending the team's next five home games after an exchange with two fans, who were sat courtside displaying signs thanking Cunningham for "speaking up for girls".

Keaton reportedly confronted the teenage fans and admonished them during the game. The Storm have since apologised.

As for Cunningham, the attention has increasingly become an unwelcome distraction.

Having defended her original comments, she said recently that she now wanted the conversation to return to what was happening on court.

"I want to get back to basketball, it's always been about basketball" she said, arguing that the standard of play in the WNBA was being overshadowed by issues away from the game.

But that may prove difficult, as pressure grows on the league to clarify exactly who is eligible to play.

In recent years, many governing bodies in sport have amended their rules about the inclusion of transgender athletes at the elite level, moving more towards restrictions.

Athletics, cycling and aquatics, for example, have implemented outright bans on transgender women taking part in women's events.

In March, it was announced that the women's category of Olympic sports will be limited to biological females from the LA Olympic Games in 2028.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) says eligibility will be determined by a "once-in-a-lifetime" sex test, which would prevent transgender women and those with differences in sexual development (DSD) who have gone through male puberty from competing.

In the United States, transgender women and girls are banned from competing in women's sports categories in schools, universities and the grassroots level.

That was part of an executive order - titled "Keeping Men Out of Women's Sports" - signed by President Trump last year.

It does not cover professional sport.

title: Don Nelson, former NBA coach and 5-time champion as a player, dies at 86
description: Don Nelson was one of two coaches in NBA history to have at least 250 wins with three different franchises — Milwaukee, Dallas and Golden State.
fullText:
Don Nelson, the NBA's three-time Coach of the Year and a five-time champion, has died at the age of 86, his family said in a statement.

"On Sunday morning our beloved husband, dad, grandfather and great-grandfather Don Nelson peacefully went to be with the Lord, surrounded by his loving family," the statement said. "Throughout his last week, friends and family encircled him with love, sharing the blessing of his friendship and revisiting treasured memories."

As a player, Nelson played 11 of his 14 seasons with the Boston Celtics, winning five NBA championships before going on to coach after he retired from playing.

He last coached for the Golden State Warriors in 2010 and retired as the NBA's winningest coach. Over his 30-year career, he coached four teams, including the Milwaukee Bucks, New York Knicks and Dallas Mavericks.

Nelson also served as general manager for all three franchises and is one of two coaches in NBA history to have at least 250 wins with the three teams.

Dallas Mavericks Governor Patrick Dumont said Nelson helped transform the franchise and brought "a winning culture" to the city.

"Don Nelson was a true original whose impact on the Dallas Mavericks and the game of basketball will endure for generations ... His influence can be seen throughout Mavericks history and across the NBA today," Dumont said.

Nelson introduced what is now known as the point forward, and his up-tempo style of offense created a buzz. He said the idea of shifting from the dominant big men of the 1970s to an offense focused on speed and the fast break came from his playing days under Celtics Hall of Fame coach Red Auerbach.

"The league really hadn't seen an offense like the one we were running, and the results were undeniable," Nelson wrote in 2016 in The Players' Tribune.

Nelson was best known for his stint in Oakland, where he drafted Stephen Curry and was credited with helping build the Warriors' ascent.

"'Nellie' was one of the most innovative and influential coaches in NBA history and an iconic figure in Warriors history. He was a true basketball visionary who saw the game differently and was never afraid to challenge conventional thinking," the Warriors said in a statement posted to social media.

Nelson will be remembered for his authenticity, personality and passion for basketball, the organization said.

In a statement, Curry said, "The story is [Nelson] never liked rookies, but from Day 1, he challenged me and gave me an opportunity to be my best self on the court ... He had an immeasurable impact on the sport and will go down as one of the greatest minds in the history of the game."

"Don Nelson revolutionized NBA basketball through his fearlessness, ingenuity and deep conviction," NBA Commissioner Adam Silver said in a statement. "He brought an unmistakable personality to everything he did, and his impact on our sport will continue to be felt for generations."

The Celtics, in a statement, highlighted Nelson's playing career and said it would be a mistake to let his coaching career overshadow his gameplay.

In Game 7 of the 1969 NBA Finals against his former team, the Los Angeles Lakers, Nelson "converted one of the most famous shots in playoff history—a foul-line jumper which dropped through the basket after hitting the back rim and bouncing several feet straight up," the organization said.

"The Celtics extend our deep condolences to Nelson's family, loved ones, and everyone he touched through his rich and impactful life in basketball and beyond," the statement said. "The shot, taken with just over a minute to go in the game and the Celtics clinging to a 103-102 lead, was an essential play in helping secure Boston's 11th NBA title in 13 seasons."

Nelson won all five of his playing titles with the Celtics, and in 1978, two years after his final season as a player, his number 19 was raised to the rafters in Boston.

In 2000, Nelson revealed a prostate cancer diagnosis and later said he had his cancerous prostate removed, with doctors having found no sign that the disease had spread.

Nelson's cause of death wasn't revealed. He is survived by his children and his wife, Joy.

A deal has to be worked out between Watson and the Denver Nuggets, which would likely come in the form of a sign-and-trade. However, with Denver in a difficult financial situation, there has been discussion about Watson potentially accepting his qualifying offer instead.

"That is why teams like the LA Clippers, Milwaukee Bucks, Cleveland Cavaliers, and Atlanta Hawks have all expressed sign-and-trade interest in Watson over the last month. The teams clearly want Watson, but the Nuggets are not going to let him leave unless they receive a package they believe is worth it.

title: Voice-cloned video falsely claims NBA coach planned to recruit late Filipino basketball player
description: T he death of young Filipino basketball player Rene Baterbonia at a training camp in June captivated social media users in the Philippines, including a TikTok post falsely claiming that an NBA coach had planned to recruit the 18-year-old for the 2026-27 season. fullText:
T he death of young Filipino basketball player Rene Baterbonia at a training camp in June captivated social media users in the Philippines, including a TikTok post falsely claiming that an NBA coach had planned to recruit the 18-year-old for the 2026-27 season. AFP found that the clip had been digitally altered, while the original video was published before Baterbonia's death.

"OKC Thunder coach planned to recruit Rene Baterbonia after seeing his potential during his basketball games," the overlaid Tagalog-language text on a TikTok clip reads.

The post has racked up over 869,000 views since it was published on July 20. It claims Baterbonia "would've been the first pure Filipino to join the NBA".

The TikTok video shows Mark Daigneault, head coach of the NBA's Oklahoma City Thunder (OKC Thunder), speaking at a press conference ( archived link).

Daigneault can be heard saying they planned to draft Baterbonia, an 18-year-old college student at Ateneo De Manila University, before he died (archived here and here).

"Over the past year, our scouts closely followed Rene Baterbonia and were impressed by his talent, work ethic, and potential," he appears to say in the clip.

"Internally, we were preparing to select him in the 2026 to 2027 NBA draft and had even discussed a multi-year contract worth approximately 25 million US dollars."

"Unfortunately, events took an unexpected turn, and those plans will never become real."

Social media users shared the same clip on TikTok and Facebook, after Baterbonia and teammate Divine Adili drowned during a team-building exercise in the eastern Philippines on June 8 ( archived link).

Their deaths and the subsequent investigation by authorities unleashed a frenzy of social media posts about Baterbonia, a promising small-town athlete recently recruited into collegiate basketball.

Officials from his hometown of Talacogon in Mindanao island released a statement on July 30, asking the public to stop soliciting financial assistance for the Baterbonia family and to stop posting visits to the basketball player's grave for content ( archived link).

But this video has been altered and the original YouTube video was published on May 31, eight days before Baterbonia's death.

A reverse image search using the clip's keyframes found the original unedited version of the video published on the OKC Thunder's official YouTube channel ( archived link).

The video's description reads: "Head Coach Mark Daigneault speaks with the media at end-of-season interviews."

Daigneault made no mention of Baterbonia in the entirety of the video.

A close inspection of the altered footage found that Daigneault's mouth did not match the audio.

Using the Hiya detection tool within the Verification Plugin found the clip's audio was "very likely AI-generated".

title: In financial move, Rockets release JD Davison from non-guaranteed deal
description: To officially dip below the NBA’s 2026-27 luxury tax line, the Houston Rockets released backup guard JD Davison. He was on a non-guaranteed contract.
fullText:
In a move designed to clear space beneath the NBA's 2026-27 luxury tax, the Rockets announced the release of backup guard JD Davison on Wednesday.

Davison's minimum contract for next season was not yet guaranteed, and the 23-year-old does not have any remaining two-way eligibility. He played most of 2025-26 on a two-way deal.

As things stand, Davison's path to a standard roster spot had become much more difficult after Houston's offseason acquisitions of Bruce Thornton and Marcus Smart, a pair of guards who played last season with Ohio State and the Los Angeles Lakers.

Davison's release does open up an additional training camp roster spot, which could be used to evaluate a non-guaranteed player who is either eligible for a two-way contract or potentially a fit for Houston's G League affiliate, the Rio Grande Valley (RGV) Vipers.

NBA teams are allowed to carry up to 21 players in the offseason and into the preseason, but that number dips to a maximum of 15 standard deals and three two-way slots for the regular season, which begins in late October.

This leaves the Rockets $14,077 under the luxury tax with 14 players.

That amount is worth one day of service for the veteran minimum.

If they don’t make any additional moves this season, they could sign a 15th player on the last day of the season and finish with $0 tax space. https://t.co/CeAZXgxUdt

As for Davison, a former G League Most Valuable Player (MVP), the 6-foot-1 guard has proven all there is to prove at that level. Thus, he's likely to seek out another NBA opportunity elsewhere.

In 28 games with the Rockets last season, Davison averaged 2.5 points in 7.8 minutes, and he was a dependable ball-handler and perimeter defender, as well.

A waiver of Davison was long considered an inevitability, especially after the Rockets drafted Bruce Thornton. It's also the answer to a very simple math problem.

title: NBA Europe will take UK to another level - Anunoby
description: The planned launch of a bespoke European NBA league has the potential to take basketball in the United Kingdom to the "next level", says the New York Knicks' OG Anunoby.
fullText:
The planned launch of a bespoke European NBA league has the potential to take basketball in the United Kingdom to the "next level", says the New York Knicks' OG Anunoby.

With the working title of NBA Europe, it is planned for launch in October 2027 and is aiming to have 16 European teams - with London and Manchester expected to be included.

The deadline for final bids to own franchises was in June and it is hoped the identities of teams that will feature will begin to be announced this year, with the NBA receiving bids between $500m (£372m) and $1bn (£745m) for each target host city.

Anunoby is the standout current player of UK origin in the NBA, having played a starring role in the Knicks' first NBA title win since 1973.

Alongside the Portland Trail Blazers' Jeremy Sochan, the Boston Celtics' Amari Williams and Tobi Lawal, who is set to make his NBA debut this season for the Dallas Mavericks, Anunoby makes up part of the NBA's UK quartet.

"I think it is amazing," Anunoby told BBC Sport when asked about the NBA Europe plans.

"Basketball continues to grow, especially here in London and in Manchester.

"It's exciting and I think it is going to take basketball to another level out here."

Plans for the league's launch in just over a year's time remain "on track", with the league set to start in tandem with the 2027-28 NBA season.

"Planning is going really well. We've had an amazing amount of demand in the last couple of months for NBA Europe, particularly as bidding closed," said Laura Pinnell, vice-president and head of Consumer Group for the NBA across Europe and the Middle East.

"I would say the UK is one of the biggest opportunities for us out of the whole project.

"The growth opportunity is incredible and actually a London franchise, there is discussion about a Manchester franchise. All of which are great opportunities for fans and also, youth and participation."

Anunoby, a two-time NBA Championship winner, has spent time in his birth city of London this week during his off-season break.

As well as investing his own money as part of a grassroots court development in Camden, Anunoby has been eyeing the prospect of helping the Knicks win a second NBA title in as many years next season.

The NBA has had eight different champions in as many years, with no team being able to produce back-to-back titles since the Golden State Warriors in 2017 and 2018.

"That's our goal this year," said Anunoby in response to the prospect of ending the run of consecutive different winners.

But asked which of the Knicks' 29 NBA rivals will pose their biggest threat, the 29-year-old said challenges will come from across the competition.

"The whole league," added Anunoby.

"It is a very tough league and every team is capable and everyone is a threat."

title: LeBron James Philadelphia 76ers Tribute Goes Viral
description: Philadelphia is already embracing LeBron James, with a new Sixers mural of the four-time NBA champion attracting attention in Fairmount. The post LeBron James Philadelphia 76ers Tribute Goes Viral appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Philadelphia muralist Bill Strobel appears to be behind the LeBron James tribute attracting attention in the city’s Fairmount section.

The completed artwork depicts James in a black Philadelphia 76ers No. 23 jersey against a red-and-blue background. Its signature, @billstro4_art, matches Strobel’s Instagram handle.

A close-up of the completed mural shows the handle @billstro4_art painted beside the image. That account belongs to Bill Strobel, a Philadelphia artist with an established connection to the city’s sports murals.

Strobel previously painted a Jalen Hurts mural in Fairmount before the Philadelphia Eagles’ Super Bowl appearance. The Eagles described that project as one Strobel initiated himself at Brown and Corinthian Streets. He has also produced artwork for Lincoln Financial Field and other prominent Philadelphia locations.

The attribution turns the Sixers mural into more than an anonymous viral tribute. It appears to be the latest work from an artist who has repeatedly used Philadelphia’s walls to mark significant moments involving the city’s teams.

The mural appeared less than a week after the Sixers officially announced that James would wear No. 23 in Philadelphia.

James, 41, joined the Sixers after eight seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers. He described the move as the final major decision of his playing career and said the opportunity to compete for another championship helped lead him to Philadelphia.

That context makes the mural more than an imaginative picture of James in another team’s uniform. He is now actually a member of the Sixers, joining a roster built around Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe.

Philadelphia has not won an NBA championship since 1983. James, meanwhile, has won four titles across three franchises. Another championship would make him the first player to win one with four different NBA teams.

The finished mural presents James in a familiar pose, wearing his trademark No. 23 with “Sixers” across his chest. Its appearance in Fairmount reflects the speed with which his signing has moved from transaction news to something Philadelphia fans can see in their own neighborhood.

James wearing a Philadelphia uniform once existed only in mock-ups and recruiting pitches.

The Sixers pursued him during the summer of 2018, when a Philadelphia contingent met with his representative, Rich Paul. James ultimately signed with the Lakers, beginning an eight-year run in Los Angeles instead.

Philadelphia’s interest was especially visible that year because billboards attempted to recruit James to the Sixers. Eight years later, he finally chose the franchise, turning those old hypothetical images into reality.

That history gives the Fairmount artwork an added layer. It is not a fan campaign trying to convince James to come to Philadelphia. It is a celebration of a move that has already happened.

James’ signing immediately raised the Sixers’ expectations, although their championship prospects will depend heavily on health, chemistry and how their collection of high-usage stars fits together. The mural captures the more optimistic side of the moment: Philadelphia has a new superstar, and the city is already making space for him.

Most of his game-worn memorabilia from major highlights of his career could be more valuable than a rookie Topps card, but if you put it all together, James could add $100 million to his net worth just by putting an actual value on these items.

James’ $5.2 million 2003 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Rookie Patch Autograph card actually cost $6.4 million to the new owner after all fees and taxes were accounted for.

If James were to sell his own personal version of the card, it’d be far more valuable because it is a verifiable belonging of James, not just a card that came out of a pack.

The most expensive sports card of all time cost $12.9 million in August 2025, a 2007–08 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Dual Logoman Autograph with both Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant.

Cards with LeBron as a rookie are bound to become more valuable in the coming years, especially after he retires from the sport.

The billionaire James can afford to play on minimum NBA contracts in his twilight due to his shrewd off-court success, so it’s unlikely he’d suddenly lose his fortune and need to sell cards and memorabilia to restart his life.

title: 3 NBA players Heat should target in trades after losing out on LeBron sweepstakes
description: This is how the Miami Heat can regroup after losing out on LeBron James.
fullText:
The Miami Heat were a frontrunner in the LeBron sweepstakes, with many people around the NBA, including their social media team, believing James was going to sign there. Instead, Miami missed out on King James.

Miami knew that after making the blockbuster deal to acquire Giannis Antetokounmpo, it had to sign another notable free agent to become a contender in the Eastern Conference.

Since LeBron waited until the end of free agency to make his decision, there aren’t many options left for Miami. Still, there are three free agents the Heat could target to establish themselves as legitimate contenders.

MORE: 3 NBA teams who are most improved entering 2026-2027 season

DeRozan was released by the Sacramento Kings earlier this offseason, and he would likely be the best fit in Miami.

DeRozan is entering his 17th NBA season and proved last year that he still has plenty left in the tank. He averaged 18 points per game in 77 games. Miami is lacking significant guard play, with its projected starting backcourt consisting of Davion Mitchell and Tim Hardaway Jr. Those players aren’t bad, but on a championship contender they’re probably better suited as depth pieces.

DeRozan has a couple of options in free agency, with several teams scrambling to make a move after LeBron signed with Philadelphia.

The Los Angeles Clippers recently traded Kawhi Leonard, signaling the start of a rebuild, so they likely won’t re-sign Bradley Beal.

Beal played just six games last season, but when healthy, he’s still an elite scorer in the league. We’re only five years removed from Beal leading the NBA in scoring at 31 points per game. It’s clear Miami needs help in the backcourt, and he could take some of the offensive burden off Giannis and Bam Adebayo.

MORE: 3 NBA teams that have quietly won the offseason already

Though Bennedict Mathurin is a restricted free agent, rumors are circulating that the Clippers are looking for sign-and-trade partners.

Mathurin is entering his fifth season and has established himself as a reliable scorer. The young guard was traded to Los Angeles last year in a deal with the Indiana Pacers. He has consistently averaged around 17 points per game throughout his young career while making slight improvements in nearly every other statistical category. Mathurin is the youngest and most athletic option, but he would also be the most difficult player for the Heat to acquire.

If the Heat want to become true contenders, Mathurin might be their best option.

title: Report: Cavaliers’ LeBron Chances Took Major Blow After Mobley Trade Decision
description: While the NBA world is still bumping with emotion over the LeBron James to Philadelphia 76ers news, the Cleveland Cavaliers are still processing what hit them.Not only did James say no to a storybook reunion, but he joined the conference rival instead. So what led to the four-time league MVP passing on a reunion when […] The post Report: Cavaliers’ LeBron Chances Took Major Blow After Mobley Trade Decision appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
While the NBA world is still bumping with emotion over the LeBron James to Philadelphia 76ers news, the Cleveland Cavaliers are still processing what hit them.

Not only did James say no to a storybook reunion, but he joined the conference rival instead. So what led to the four-time league MVP passing on a reunion when many were convinced that was his best path forward?

According to NBA insider Brett Siegel, the Cavs decision to not trade for Jaylen Brown likely played a major role in James saying no to Cleveland.

“The issue of the Cavaliers not making any moves to improve their roster, specifically not pursuing Jaylen Brown when Boston was making him available, also clearly influenced James’ decision. If Cleveland was willing to part ways with Evan Mobley in a deal for Brown, that would’ve weighed heavily in LeBron’s mind, but this is simply a hypothetical game at this juncture.”

LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – FEBRUARY 22: Jaylen Brown #7 of the Boston Celtics attempts a shot against LeBron James #23 of the Los Angeles Lakers during the first half of their game at Crypto.com Arena on February 22, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Luiza Moraes/Getty Images)

The Cavs thought they were sitting pretty by not making any moves. They wanted to preserve all the flexibility needed to add James to the roster and, perhaps, pay him significantly more than what competing teams could offer.

Instead, they may have been watching their chances to land The King quickly fade away as James held back to see which teams were making big moves.

The Sixers pulled the trigger. They landed Brown, the 29-year-old perennial All-Star, from the Boston Celtics in a stunning, and rather lopsided, trade.

Clearly, that move caught James’ eyes and ears. According to ESPN’s Shams Charania, the Sixers did not register on James’ radar until they acquired Brown.

“Philadelphia, I’m telling you was not even on this radar, was not in the pool of candidates until Bob Myers went out and got Jaylen Brown that changed the equation,” Charania said on ESPN’s First Take Friday morning following James’ move to the Sixers. “The Sixers got on the map and from there it became for LeBron James now almost four weeks of deliberation with LeBron James, Rich Paul, that inner circle there and his family, eventually.”

HOUSTON, TEXAS – MARCH 16: LeBron James #23 of the Los Angeles Lakers looks on during the National Anthem prior to the game against the Houston Rockets at Toyota Center on March 16, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images)

The day after the James news was announced, ESPN’s Brian Windhorst laid out the three biggest reasons why James chose Philadelphia over Cleveland.

“In the end, there were three strikes against Cleveland: Family not being an issue in LeBron’s choice, the front office not making a deal for (Jaylen) Brown and the Cavs’ roster not featuring (Darius) Garland. To say it was one of these factors more than the other might be missing the big picture,” Windhorst wrote.

Garland, James’ fellow Klutch Sports client, was moved to the Los Angeles Clippers for James Harden in a trade in February. Windhorst believes the Cavs’ decision to move Garland, with whom James has a strong relationship, is another reason why James didn’t return to Cleveland.

If that is also true, then it boils down to this: the Cavs lost James months before he ever signed with the 76ers. The Garland trade in February started the slide, and not making a move for Brown this summer became the final blow.

title: ‘Truly a Joke’ — NBA World Rips Warriors Owner Joe Lacob’s Controversial Decision to Focus on ‘Post-Steph Curry Era’
description: The Golden State Warriors’ offseason plan to give Stephen Curry another shot at the championship did not go as planned. After LeBron James decided to take his talents to Philadelphia, Warriors insider Tim Kawakami reported on Saturday that team governor Joe Lacob has shifted his focus past the Curry era.
fullText:
The Golden State Warriors’ offseason plan to give Stephen Curry another shot at the championship did not go as planned. After LeBron James decided to take his talents to Philadelphia, Warriors insider Tim Kawakami reported on Saturday that team governor Joe Lacob has shifted his focus past the Curry era.

Unsurprisingly, Kawakami’s report sparked a major buzz in the NBA world.

The Warriors’ offseason began with grand visions of landing James after Draymond Green declined a $27.7 million player option to create salary-cap flexibility.

The plan met a major snag as the former Los Angeles Lakers superstar reportedly wanted the Warriors to sign Washington Wizards center Anthony Davis, whom the Wizards were unwilling to trade.

Still, the allure of joining forces with Curry delayed James’ decision before the four-time MVP eventually signed with the Philadelphia 76ers on Friday.

From trying to build a legendary lineup, Lacob has seemingly quit on the Warriors’ franchise icon. According to Kawakami, the billionaire will rebuild in the “post-Steph Curry era.”

The viral report drew strong reactions from the WNBA community.

“What a shame. Steph Curry is still one of the best players in the world. To not make an effort to win another title with him is truly a joke. And if you’re not gonna do that, then you have to trade him. Instead, the Warriors are just wasting Steph’s final years. So sad,” NBA analyst Kevin O’Connor tweeted.

“Stephen Curry gets to finish his career where and when he wants. The Warriors can’t trade him unless he asks them to. But in pure basketball terms, it’s better for everyone if he asks for a trade. Golden State’s window is closed, and he’s too good for an extended retirement tour,” CBS Sports’ Sam Quinn added.

“Bro, they doing Steph dirty like that,” an X user wrote.

“They wasted the last 7 years just lucked into 1 championship, so it’s not talked about,” another X user added.

“Joe Lacob has been trying to build post Steph for 8 years now. He brought in a bunch of draft picks (that all sucked) for a post Steph era only for Steph to win the Championship despite this,” another user added.

With James going East, the Warriors’ biggest offseason move left is likely re-signing Green.

After retaining Kristaps Porzingis and De’Anthony Melton and adding Charles Bassey, Golden State’s roster is practically set for the 2026-27 season.

So, the Warriors, which finished this past season with a 37-45 record, will start the new campaign without Butler and Moses Moody. While both rehab from injuries, the Dubs are desperately hoping the oft-injured Porzingis stays healthy, the 40-year-old Al Horford provides quality minutes, and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg contributes.

Meanwhile, the Oklahoma City Thunder are stronger than ever and are looking to regain their crown. The San Antonio Spurs not only gained valuable playoff experience but also retooled.

Other contenders like the Lakers and Minnesota Timberwolves have also made major offseason moves, making the stacked West even more competitive.

Lacob is essentially asking the 38-year-old Curry to keep a hobbled, aging roster afloat, a rinse-and-repeat situation that has often ended in disappointment for the superstar point guard and the team.

Until Curry retires or asks for a trade, this could be the familiar scenario Dubs Nation will be looking at.

title: ‘Not Fair to This Fan Base’ – NBA Analysts Rip Cavaliers’ Offseason ‘Failure’ After LeBron James Free-Agency Snub
description: LeBron James made it clear that his top priority in choosing his next team was the opportunity to compete for championships and experience winning again, with financial considerations playing no role in his decision. That created a realistic opening for the Cleveland Cavaliers amid their salary-cap limitations, but they were unable to capitalize on it, leaving questions about the team’s disappointing offseason.
fullText:
LeBron James made it clear that his top priority in choosing his next team was the opportunity to compete for championships and experience winning again, with financial considerations playing no role in his decision.

That created a realistic opening for the Cleveland Cavaliers amid their salary-cap limitations, but they were unable to capitalize on it, leaving questions about the team’s disappointing offseason.

Several explanations have emerged for why the Cavaliers were unable to secure James, who began his NBA career in Cleveland before returning for a second stint.

Many expected the Akron, Ohio, native to return, but the 41-year-old made it clear that family considerations did not influence his decision, and he ultimately signed with the Philadelphia 76ers.

ESPN analyst Brian Windhorst explicitly mentioned two more reasons for the Cavaliers’ failure in James’ pursuit.

The first was that the Cavaliers’ front office did not trade for Jaylen Brown. Adding a player of Brown’s caliber could have heavily changed James’ perception of the Cavaliers’ championship outlook.

As Windhorst reported, Cleveland also dealt away Darius Garland to acquire James Harden. As Garland was represented by Klutch Sports, keeping him could have helped create a more favorable environment for a reunion.

DON’T MISS: LeBron James Rumors: Eastern Conference Contender Rejected NBA Legend’s Interest Before 76ers Move

As free agency progressed, Cleveland remained largely inactive, seemingly preserving roster flexibility in hopes of landing James.

That cautious approach ultimately backfired, triggering analyst Earl D Mauldin to criticize the team’s offseason strategy.

“That’s distasteful to hear that was why you were in a holding pattern,” Mauldin said on 92.3 The Fan.

“Why the hell were you not more active making moves prior to this? Like, if you really felt in your heart that it was a possibility, but your possibility wasn’t that strong… That’s not fair to this fan base.”

“When Dan Gilbert said that we are nowhere close to where we need to be, and we will be dug in all summer doing whatever we can to improve this roster, that don’t sound like the Cavaliers was dug in all summer doing whatever they can.”

However, Cleveland could still make a big move by acquiring Jonathan Kuminga in a potential deal.

Cavaliers head coach Kenny Atkinson previously coached Kuminga with the Golden State Warriors, making a reunion in Cleveland a realistic possibility that could help energize a frustrated fan base after a quiet offseason.

MORE: ‘There Were 3 Strikes Against Cleveland’ — ESPN’s Brian Windhorst Reveals Why LeBron James Chose 76ers Over Cavaliers

Co-host Spencer German also labeled the Cavaliers’ offseason a disappointment but believes the team still has time to reshape the narrative.

“Right now, this offseason can’t be called anything but a failure…yes, they have more time to see what they can do,” German said. “We might walk away feeling better, maybe not as good as we’d feel if LeBron was here..But we might walk away feeling better about the state of things right now if they get Kuminga or they trade for somebody.”

“But as things stand right now, they’ve failed to improve this roster while other teams in the conference have gotten better.”

So far, Cleveland’s biggest offseason move has been signing Donovan Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million extension.

However, after parting ways with Dean Wade, Keon Ellis, and Larry Nance Jr., the Cavaliers still have work to do to improve a roster that finished 52-30 last season before being swept by the New York Knicks in the Eastern Conference Finals.

title: Brandon Jennings Is Right: Jayson Tatum Took a Shot at Jaylen Brown
description: Jaylen Brown remained at the center of NBA conversation after the Boston Celtics sent him to the Philadelphia 76ers in a trade built around Paul George. Criticism of Boston’s return soon created a more personal question: Did the Celtics decide they could no longer manage Brown’s personality?Jayson Tatum then delivered a leadership lesson at an […] The post Brandon Jennings Is Right: Jayson Tatum Took a Shot at Jaylen Brown appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Jaylen Brown remained at the center of NBA conversation after the Boston Celtics sent him to the Philadelphia 76ers in a trade built around Paul George. Criticism of Boston’s return soon created a more personal question: Did the Celtics decide they could no longer manage Brown’s personality?

Jayson Tatum then delivered a leadership lesson at an event for The Jayson Tatum Foundation that sounded remarkably connected to the debate surrounding his former teammate, Yahoo reports.

“Being around somebody that feels like they know it all, I don’t wanna be around that person,” Tatum said. “I don’t wanna be the smartest person in the room, I want to learn from somebody else.”

Brandon Jennings did not accept that statement as generic guidance for young players. After reposting the clip on X, Jennings wrote, “Motivational message my a-s lmaooo that’s a shot at Jaylen Brown.”

Tatum never mentioned Brown, leaving room for another explanation. Still, Jennings’ conclusion fits the timing and familiar language too well to dismiss.

Motivational message my ass lmaooo that’s a shot at Jaylen Brown https://t.co/y7m1mcZpuW

— Brandon Jennings (@Tuff__Crowd) July 25, 2026

Fox Sports host Colin Cowherd previously said two NBA sources characterized Brown as a difficult locker room presence because of how highly he regards his own intelligence.

“He suddenly thinks he’s the smartest guy in every room he’s in,” Cowherd said. “You get into a really bad place.”

Brown rejected Cowherd’s premise during a livestream after the trade, USA Today reports. The 29-year-old argued that intelligence takes different forms and said he never viewed himself as the smartest person present. He then questioned the intellectual standard across the sports business.

“No offense to everybody in sports, but the bar is fu—– low,” Brown said. “You know what I mean. The bar isn’t that high.”

Brown aimed that criticism broadly, not specifically at Tatum. However, Tatum’s choice to warn against someone who “feels like they know it all,” then invoke the same smartest-person framing, made the comparison unavoidable.

Could Brown’s comment have irritated Tatum? No public statement proves it. Their separation still changes the dynamic. Brown no longer needs to smooth over every ambiguous remark for Boston’s locker room, and Tatum does not have to seek reassurance from a teammate who now plays for a conference rival.

Without that clarification, Tatum can interpret Brown’s words however he wants. Jennings merely said aloud what many viewers heard beneath the motivational packaging.

The basketball backdrop gives this exchange more weight. Tatum’s Achilles rehabilitation limited him to 16 regular-season appearances after the injury he sustained during the 2024-25 playoffs. He returned late and participated in Boston’s postseason run, apart from Game 7 against Philadelphia.

Brown carried a leading role during Tatum’s absence. Across 71 games, he set career highs with 28.7 points, 6.9 rebounds and 5.1 assists per contest. Brown also made the All-Star team, earned Second Team All-NBA recognition and ranked No. 6 in the MVP race.

That individual success did not produce Boston’s desired ending. The Celtics surrendered a 3-1 advantage against the 76ers, the team Brown later joined, and the collapse intensified scrutiny of his leadership as a primary option.

Tatum’s remarks do not confirm that he blamed Brown for Boston’s problems. They do, however, sound like a pointed response to the criticism that followed Brown out of Boston. Of every way Tatum could have discussed leadership, he selected language already attached to the loudest conversation about his former co-star.

That is why Jennings is right about the subtext. Until Tatum offers a different explanation, every Celtics-76ers meeting will invite another look at whether their long-running partnership ended with more friction than either star has acknowledged.

title: ‘YOU JOINED THE EAST FAVORITES!’ – Skip Bayless Accuses LeBron James of ‘Ring Chasing’ After 76ers Move
description: Skip Bayless joined the NBA world in reacting to LeBron James’ decision on Friday to join the Philadelphia 76ers. The talk show host, a known and unapologetic critic of the former Los Angeles Lakers superstar, wasted little time in sharing his thoughts about James signing a two-year, $8 million deal to play in Philly.
fullText:
Skip Bayless joined the NBA world in reacting to LeBron James’ decision on Friday to join the Philadelphia 76ers. The talk show host, a known and unapologetic critic of the former Los Angeles Lakers superstar, wasted little time in sharing his thoughts about James signing a two-year, $8 million deal to play in Philly.

As usual, Bayless didn’t hold back after James ended his three-week hold-up in free agency by going to a team loaded with talent.

The 76ers were reportedly not on James’ radar until they acquired Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics. Without giving up VJ Edgecombe or Tyrese Maxey, Philadelphia now has a stacked core that is as good, if not better, than any NBA team.

After nearly a month of speculation, the 22-time All-Star snubbed the Miami Heat, Golden State Warriors, Minnesota Timberwolves, and Cleveland Cavaliers, the other frontrunners to get his signature.

A few hours after news broke that James is now a 76er, Bayless reacted.

“CONGRATS, LEBRON! YOU MADE THE OBVIOUS RING-CHASING CHOICE! YOU JOINED THE EAST FAVORITES!” Bayless tweeted.

On Friday’s “The Skip Bayless Show,” the veteran sports journalist added more context to his message.

“This wasn’t about basketball happiness! … This was about ring chasing. What team gave LeBron James the best chance to win a fifth, maybe even a sixth championship? It was obviously from the start the Philadelphia 76ers,” Bayless said.

According to Bayless, the 41-year-old superstar wouldn’t take his talents to the Golden State Warriors, which the podcaster named the “Olden State,” if James had gone there.

Bayless continued that he didn’t predict the Timberwolves to win the James sweepstakes, as the 21-time All-NBA wouldn’t want to live in Minneapolis.

The Cavaliers offered a storybook ending, but Bayless didn’t see this version of James as the right fit on that roster.

For the former Fox Sports talk show host, the “happiness” driven decision for James would have been to take his talents back to South Beach, where he could compete for a championship and play golf “all year round.”

The allure of returning to a place where he won two championships and where Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo now lead the roster was not enough to sway James.

MORE: ‘Legacy-Wise, It Didn’t Add Up’ – LeBron James’ Former Teammate Questions NBA Legend’s $8 Million 76ers Deal

Bayless said that it was a no-brainer for James to choose Philadelphia after the 76ers pulled off what he called the “steal of the century” by getting Brown.

The analyst also argued that Maxey and VJ Edgecombe provide enviable youth and speed to surround a player entering his 24th NBA season.

Finally, there is Joel Embiid, who, when healthy, Bayless called the closest the NBA has seen to a Shaquille O’Neal.

Bayless’ criticism of James isn’t new or surprising. Over the past few years, he has been taking shots at the Akron, Ohio, native’s championships, claiming they were won by stacking his teams.

James likely knew he would be criticized regardless of which team he chose to play for. Bayless took his shots, but the only thing that matters to the 76ers’ brand-new acquisition is a chance to win championship No. 5.

title: NBA best & worst offseason moves now that LeBron is in Philly
description: The best and the worst moves of the offseason.
fullText:
The entire NBA world has been patiently awaiting LeBron James’ decision. Now that he has decided to team up with Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown in Philadelphia, all of the big names have signed. That means each team’s roster is, for the most part, finalized.

Whether it has been a blockbuster trade or a superstar signing elsewhere, there have been numerous major moves this offseason. Some of those moves propelled teams into championship contention, while others pushed teams further away from it. Regardless, it’s time to look at the best and worst moves of the offseason.

MORE: NBA world reacts to LeBron James’ stunning 76ers decision

LeBron may have lost a step, but he is still one of the best playmakers in the NBA. James averaged 21 points, 6 rebounds and 7 assists this past season and was a top free agent this summer. Philadelphia already looked like one of the top teams in the NBA, and this move was the cherry on top.

In April, Philadelphia was playing in the play-in tournament. Now, it’s the championship favorite.

Minnesota has been searching for a guard and finally got one, and it isn’t just an average one either. Ball now teams up with Anthony Edwards, and the two are poised to become one of the deadliest backcourts in the NBA.

Philadelphia acquiring Jaylen Brown has to be the top move of the offseason.

Boston traded Brown to Philadelphia in a blockbuster deal this offseason. Brown is coming off an MVP-caliber season in which he led Boston to the second seed in the East. The 76ers got younger and improved at the small forward position.

On top of that, Philadelphia was able to keep V.J. Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey in the trade.

MORE: 3 NBA teams that have quietly won the offseason already

Miami acquires Giannis Antetokounmpo

A player of Antetokounmpo’s caliber can’t hurt a team, but Miami did give up its supporting cast and future for the superstar. The Heat now have no significant players outside of Giannis and Bam.

A failed attempt to sign LeBron leaves the Heat in shambles. Miami went from a play-in team to… a play-in team.

LaMelo was the only bright spot on the Hornets for years and played a huge role in the team’s best season in a decade. Yet they still traded him for Naz Reid. They re-signed Coby White to take his place. White provides scoring but is a far worse playmaker than Ball.

The Hornets took a clear step back with this trade.

Ja Morant looked like one of the best players in the league just a couple of seasons ago before the injuries and off-court issues. Memphis finally traded him this offseason for older players, leaving top-three pick Cameron Boozer with a poor supporting cast.

The Grizzlies didn’t get younger, nor did they improve. It feels like they’re setting their rookie up for failure.

fullText:
